discovery.summary: The epicenter is the immutable Diagram revision model plus CanvasHistory and MappingDocumentController. Browser editing, agent commands, isolated generation, change proposals, and evaluations converge on these structures. Eleven selected points capture that shared core, its persistence boundary, and its principal consumers.

points.title: Immutable Diagram Model
points.rationale: Diagram combines versioned ASCII content, parsed nodes, source evidence, highlights, and jumps. Revision operations preserve logical node identities while validating edits. This is the fundamental value shared by rendering, agents, history, and storage; parser versions also protect existing node references.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: CanvasHistory separates diagram revision bindings from composition, personal view state, and saved CanvasViews. MappingDocumentController applies version-checked semantic operations and coordinates checkpoints, alternatives, transfers, and navigation. Browser sessions and isolated server-side canvases reuse this boundary.

relationships.label: binds immutable revisions into canvas checkpoints

points.title: Interactive Canvas Editor
points.rationale: MappingPage assembles the workspace and command receivers. CanvasSession publishes committed state through focused stores, while the tldraw runtime owns live geometry and native undo navigation. Settled gestures become controller commands; rendering, selection, and routing derive from the same semantic document.

relationships.label: commits semantic edits and restores checkpoints
submits workspace changes and flushes acknowledged mutations
opens mapped source through repository services

points.title: Durable Canvas Persistence
points.rationale: Persistence separates immutable diagram/checkpoint records from mutable catalogs and workspace manifests. Browser-side change tracking sends record batches rather than complete histories. Server adapters validate versions and retry receipts, write referenced records first, and publish manifests or catalogs afterward.

relationships.label: stores and restores checkpoint graphs and workspace records
persists immutable revisions behind content-addressed references

points.title: HTTP and MCP Boundary
points.rationale: The Vite adapter exposes application services through HTTP, streaming responses, and live sockets. Bootstrap is the concrete composition root. The MCP server translates tool calls into these HTTP endpoints, making this the principal external access boundary rather than a separate implementation of canvas behavior.

relationships.label: dispatches canvas tools and attaches live readers
exposes chat and generation operations
serves source files and definition lookups
exposes workspace batches and canvas publication
exposes proposal workflows and push intake
exposes evaluation and comparison services

points.title: Live Canvas Agent Protocol
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService binds tools to specific canvases and documents, validates requests, and manages retry-safe execution. Commands travel through a polling bridge to the browser; a separate live service distributes selection/context updates over sockets. Compact projections and revision guards keep agent references tied to the correct state.

relationships.label: dispatches bound browser commands and receives live state
redirects scoped reads and mutations into proposal sessions
uploads and resolves scoped agent context

points.title: Agent Chat and Generation
points.rationale: Agent Chat manages persistent conversations, native Codex events, tool bindings, and independent canvas alternatives. Diagram edit and batch services validate generated revisions before application. Codex stdio and Pi runtimes are distinct execution adapters; GenerationCanvasBridge gives child generations isolated controllers using the normal canvas command contract.

relationships.label: invokes canvas tools through bound sessions
creates isolated controllers for generated alternatives
validates and submits generated revision edits
reuses captured conversations and pinned source context

points.title: Reusable Agent Context
points.rationale: AgentContext captures immutable conversation trajectories and source constituents. The library adds durable identities, lineage, grouping, and retry-safe creation; transient uploads remain workspace/document scoped. Diagram-bound contexts and source snapshots make this a shared input boundary for edits, chat alternatives, and evaluations.

relationships.label: captures source ranges from registered corpus bindings
stores shared immutable source blobs
compiles contexts from diagram evidence and revision identity

points.title: Repository Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves an explicit diagram or source binding rather than assuming one repository per project. Corpus providers handle filesystem reads, the repository registry handles Git identities, and optional language services resolve definitions. Browser repository and source panes consume this boundary to connect diagrams back to code.

relationships.label: resolves mappings, evidence, and source bindings
loads registered sources and saved representation bindings

points.title: Repository Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped canvases and Git hunks into isolated proposals, applies the shared controller operations, and retains baseline/proposed history for review. Acceptance checks captured versions before atomic catalog publication. DiffSession workflows and deduplicated push intake feed this same proposal lifecycle.

relationships.label: forks histories and applies shared controller operations
publishes accepted canvases and recovery receipts
uses agent tools during proposal materialization

points.title: Evaluation and Comparison Workflows
points.rationale: Evaluation runs pin prompt versions, contexts, and canvas checkpoints before generation. Materializers turn validated results into canvas outputs; comparison sessions preserve independent input copies. Experiments, judgements, and promotion build on these records, making this a substantial consumer of the shared model rather than a parallel diagram system.

relationships.label: pins and materializes independent canvas histories
loads immutable generation inputs
publishes promoted outputs into project catalogs
reconciles chat-generated alternatives into evaluation records
captures proposal sessions as evaluation outputs

limitations: Review depth varies. reviewedPaths includes files inspected through source declarations, imports, test names/assertions, or other excerpts; it does not mean every file was read in full. Central definitions and callers were traced in greater detail.

Many implementation and test bodies remain uninspected, particularly peripheral UI components, styles, benchmark/browser harnesses, migration scripts, projection-3d, and Python parser experiments. This is a global architectural assessment, not an exhaustive code audit.
The offline static-analysis subsystem and supporting tooling were considered but omitted from the selected epicenter. Their omission does not imply they are unused.

Assessment is limited to the working-tree snapshot captured at 2026-11-11T05:54:36.232538+00:00, based on head 8ca143700ca4d2c870f1101b8cd4601ab68abd41. Index exclusions include corpus, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor, node_modules, most documentation, binary/assets, and lockfiles.

No live repository, external sources, or existing diagram presentation was used to establish the architecture. Tests and runtime integrations were not executed; relationships reflect inspected source.

|   |   `-- Validate binding, annotations, mapping geometry, evidence, and joins

|   |   |   `-- Match unique node by line, columns, and label
|   |   |-- Explicit claim: existing logical ref -> one output node at a line
|   |   `-- Reject conflicting claims or multiple identities claiming one node
|   |-- Scoped replacement [diagramSubtreeEdit.ts]
|   |   |-- Resolve revision-pinned roots; reject stale or noncontiguous subtrees
|   |   |-- Single subtree, multiple contiguous, or multiple disjoint ranges

|   |   `-- Candidate supplies full ASCII context

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 93 to 60 lines (35.5%) and from 6,203 to 4,047 characters (34.8%). Five peripherals expand meaningful concept lines: evidence dependencies, parser calls, revision ownership, scoped edits, and connection continuity. Modular boundaries are grouped by responsibility rather than file location. Positions use measured text dimensions with at least 12 columns between diagram groups.

Grounding: evidence comes from diagram.ts; parsing from diagramContent.ts, diagramContentNodes.ts, asciiTree.ts, asciiGraph/parseAsciiGraph.ts, and interpreter/index.ts; revision ownership from diagramRevision.ts, diagramRevisionEditor.ts, and diagramRevisionStore.ts; edit scope from diagramSubtreeEdit.ts; connections from diagramConnection.ts. All are supplied sources under domain/core/diagrams/.

The seed is largely supported, with two qualifications. Its rejection of noncontiguous subtrees applies to each selected subtree: diagramReplacementRanges explicitly permits multiple disjoint selections. Its durable-flushing statement is an adapter contract documented in diagramRevisionStore.ts, not an implementation demonstrated by the supplied files. The diagrams also distinguish service revisions from content revisions: annotation and source-mapping edits preserve the local content revision while reviseDiagram issues a new service revision for a changed payload.

Additional source-grounded detail includes source ID derivation and search fields, interpreter stages, frame borders excluded from graph wires, graph edges omitted from the content-node projection, cloned views, empty replacement intervals, and the precise stale-anchor validation exception. Uncertainty remains around imported construction, patching, registry, and durable-adapter implementations because they were not supplied. Subtree range calculation is shown as implemented using node anchor lines and root fold ranges; it does not establish full multiline-span coverage.

Immutable Diagram Model - shared value for canvas, agents, history, storage
|-- Diagram: repository-independent payload
|   |-- diagramId: stable service identity; revisionId: service revision
|   |-- id + revision: local canvas key + nonnegative content revision
|   |-- content: ASCII + SHA-256 + content revisionId + versioned structure
|   |-- sourceContext: contentHash + mappings + evidence + optional binding
|   |   |-- mapping.entityId + sourceRangeIndex -> evidence -> source range
|   |   `-- diagramSource(): entries, selection, and search through one join
|   `-- Optional highlights and jumps
|-- Content interpretation
|   |-- buildDiagramContent(ascii, revisionId, kind, version)
|   |   |-- Up to 20000 printable ASCII characters with LF newlines
|   |   `-- Blank content allowed only as a rectangular diagram placeholder
|   |-- Tree content stores rootIds, nodes, hierarchy, and foldRanges
|   |   |-- New trees use ascii-tree-2; ascii-tree-1 remains supported
|   |   |-- parseAsciiTree -> parseDiagram with strict tree options
|   |   `-- Node ID = content revisionId + ASCII hash + line number
|   |-- Diagram content derives nodes through a pinned parser
|   |   |-- ascii-graph-1 -> parseAsciiGraph -> boxes projected as nodes
|   |   |-- Missing parserVersion -> legacy mixed parseDiagram
|   |   `-- Derived nodes are frozen and cached by content object
|   `-- Rebuilds retain parser version to protect stored nodeRefs
|-- Revision lifecycle
|   |-- createDiagram -> prepareCreate -> issue immutable revision
|   |-- reviseDiagram -> prepareEdit; unchanged object returns base
|   |   |-- source-mappings: expectedContentHash must match
|   |   |-- patch / patches: line-range edits and optional correspondence
|   |   |-- replace: content revision + 1; rebase previous annotations
|   |   `-- highlights / jumps: validate replacement annotations
|   |-- deriveDiagram: reuse refs from supplied same-diagram revisions
|   |   `-- Each claimed ref must identify exactly one output node by line
|   |-- Private issueDiagramRevision preserves diagramId; links a base parent
|   |   |-- nodeRefs: revision-scoped content node -> logical identity
|   |   |-- Reuse derived identity or proven correspondence; else new UUID
|   |   `-- Deep-freeze revision and payload; validate diagram
|   `-- resolve(contextId, diagramId): bindings -> revision -> cloned view
|       `-- Expose logical IDs in nodes, hierarchy, and active jump sources
|-- Edit integrity and continuity
|   |-- validateDiagram requires service identities and canonical content
|   |   |-- Rebuild with pinned parser; require exact serialized equality
|   |   |-- sourceContext.contentHash must equal SHA-256(content.ascii)
|   |   `-- Validate binding, annotations, mappings, evidence, and joins
|   |-- Whole-content matching requires identical ASCII and kind
|   |   |-- Match a unique node by line, columns, and label
|   |   `-- Explicit ref-to-line claims must be unambiguous and consistent
|   |-- Scoped replacement: revision-pinned roots -> selected line ranges
|   |   |-- Each subtree must be contiguous; multiple disjoint roots allowed
|   |   `-- Full-context candidate must preserve every unselected line
|   `-- merge: baseline/current binding change -> MERGE_REQUIRED
|       `-- No automatic three-way merge; otherwise copy proposed bindings
`-- Consumers and storage boundaries
    |-- Connections pin display box, content node, and content revision
    |   |-- Source is content-node; target is content-node or box
    |   |-- Strict checks require current nodes; bulk loading allows stale revisions
    |   `-- Reconcile: remove missing boxes; rebase proven matches or keep stale
    `-- Runtime revision store explicitly retains domain results
        |-- Domain create/revise/derive work without the store
        |-- Import requires a nonempty, unique logical ref per content node
        |-- Retain registers revision; get/list expose retained records/summaries
        `-- Adapter contract: flush revisions before publishing bindings

Source evidence: joins and validation
|-- Binding defines the external source boundary
|   |-- source-code pairs with git-worktree
|   |-- document pairs with filesystem-documents
|   |-- corpus.root must be an absolute Unix or Windows path
|   `-- sourceBindingFromLocation derives sourceId
|       `-- 'source-' + first 24 SHA-256 hex chars of kind + ':' + root
|-- Mappings depend on evidence, indexed by entityId
|   |-- sourceRangeIndex selects the entry's source range
|   |-- Supplied truthy sourceRangeId must match the selected range ID
|   `-- When both exist, evidence.sourceId must match binding.sourceId
|-- Evidence ranges retain source text
|   |-- Path cannot start with '/' or contain a '..' path segment
|   |-- Positive ordered line bounds; originalLines count must match
|   `-- Validation checks shape, not the current external file contents
`-- diagramSource -> queryDiagramSourceContext
    |-- entries(): map every mapping to entity, range, and binding
    |-- forSelection(rect): filter mappings, then perform the same join
    `-- search(): case-insensitive substring match
        `-- entityId, entity label, range path, or range symbol

Parser boundaries: ASCII -> addressable content nodes
|-- buildDiagramContent selects and pins a parser
|   |-- Blank placeholder: diagram kind, >1 equal-width space-only rows
|   `-- Rebuilding canonical content uses local id + ':' + revision
|-- Tree projection calls parseDiagram
|   |-- Tree dialect; zero tolerances; separate continuations; no repairs
|   |-- Stored fold range ends before next peer, or at final ASCII line
|   `-- visibleContentLines hides ranges; unknown collapsed ID is stale
|-- Shared interpreter call sequence
|   |-- policyFor validates options and freezes policy
|   |-- normalizeSource -> recognize -> interpretLayout
|   |-- interpretTrees -> interpretWires -> result
|   `-- explainNode exposes decisions, repairs, and unresolved evidence
|-- ascii-graph-1 uses its own parseAsciiGraph pipeline
|   |-- Recognize frames, branches, wires, and labels; segment text
|   |-- Assemble boxes and containment; frame borders never carry edges
|   |-- Connect wire cells; infer endpoints and deduplicate edges
|   `-- Return boxes, edges, rootIds; coordinates are 1-based inclusive
`-- diagramContentNodes exposes a narrower projection
    |-- Graph boxes -> hierarchy + per-line spans; graph edges omitted
    |-- Graph local ID uses first span's line and column
    |-- Prefix local IDs with content revisionId and ASCII hash
    |-- Missing version uses legacy mixed interpreter projection
    `-- Private WeakMap caches frozen derived nodes by content object

Revision ownership: public operations and private state
|-- Public create / revise / derive prepare domain results
|   |-- Internal construction and patch helpers are imported dependencies
|   |-- source-mappings clones supplied mappings, evidence, and binding
|   `-- Annotation/source edits preserve local content revision
|       `-- reviseDiagram still issues a new service revision if changed
|-- Private issueDiagramRevision creates the immutable record
|   |-- parentId exists only when a base revision was supplied
|   |-- Reverse proven nodeIds to find each output node's predecessor
|   |-- Logical ID precedence: derived identity, inherited ref, new UUID
|   `-- deepFreeze(record) -> validateDiagram(payload) -> return result
|-- Editor receives revisions and a context-binding callback
|   |-- Private revision lookup rejects missing or mismatched local IDs
|   `-- resolve returns a structured clone, not the stored payload
|       `-- Active jump sources omit revisionId and contentHash
`-- Store boundary explicitly retains results
    |-- createStored / reviseStored / deriveStored call retain
    |-- retain -> import -> registry.register -> registry.get
    |-- Import checks logical refs for all current content nodes
    |-- list returns frozen identity/parent summaries
    `-- Registry lifetime and durable adapter behavior are not supplied

Scoped edits: selection -> ranges -> validated patches
|-- diagramSubtreeRange resolves a current content node
|   |-- Visit childIds with a set to avoid repeated traversal
|   |-- End = max descendant anchor line and root fold-range end
|   `-- Any unrelated node inside that interval rejects the subtree
|-- diagramReplacementRanges validates the requested mode
|   |-- diagram: no subtree targets; return no restricted ranges
|   |-- subnode-single: one target; multi modes: at least two
|   |-- Pin targets to content.revisionId; sort and reject overlaps
|   |-- multi-contiguous: only blank gaps; combine into one range
|   `-- multi-disjoint: reject directly adjacent line ranges
`-- scopedReplacements checks full candidate ASCII
    |-- One range can infer its output interval from preserved context
    |-- Otherwise require one ordered output range per input range
    |-- Empty output interval uses endLine = startLine - 1
    |-- All gaps and trailing lines must match the input exactly
    `-- Return patches plus outputRanges; scope checking does not apply them

Connection continuity: validate, then reconcile
|-- Anchor schema defines endpoint capabilities
|   |-- Source: content-node; target: content-node or box
|   |-- side defaults to auto; optional offset lies within [0,1]
|   `-- Labels accept a string or text with optional pixel position
|-- connectionBox resolves 'grid:' IDs recursively through containers
|-- validateConnectionAnchor always requires an existing box
|   |-- Content-node anchors additionally require a diagram box
|   |-- allowStale bypasses node lookup only when revisions differ
|   `-- Matching revision still requires a current content node
|-- validateConnections parses <=2000 edges and rejects duplicate IDs
|   `-- Checks both anchors with allowStale = true
`-- reconcileConnections follows conservative continuity rules
    |-- Missing source or target box removes the edge
    |-- Box anchors remain unchanged
    |-- Already-stale anchors are not advanced to the newest revision
    |-- Proven nodeIds mapping rebases to a current node
    |-- Same ASCII and kind permit fallback by line and startColumn
    `-- Without a match, retain the old anchor; it can remain stale

The central tree shrinks from 127 to 84 lines (33.9%) and from 8,345 to 6,009 characters (28.0%). Five peripheral trees expand meaningful concept nodes. Modular boundaries remain visible through public capabilities and private helpers; call sequences explain writes and reconstruction; ownership explains caches, queues and disposal; data dependencies explain reference maps and publication order.

Source-grounded corrections and qualifications: canvasCatalogStore.ts passes ALL catalog revision histories to sourceBindings, which reads each history's head, rather than only current representation revisions. WorkspaceRecordStore.read reads every manifest blob on a cache miss; history=current narrows validation, not disk reads. CanvasCatalogStore parses checkpoint requests before entering its serialization queue. Workspace mutation queues are module-local and keyed by root; catalog serialization is per instance, so cross-process exclusion is not established. The catalog's writeJsonAtomic implementation is not supplied, so its fsync behavior cannot be inferred from publishJson. DiagramRevisionStore explicitly lacks fsync calls.

Peripheral additions absent from the seed include reversible checkpoint diffs and identity-sensitive restore caching (canvasCheckpointRecords.ts), disposal responsibilities and replacement projection after worker restart (workspacePersistence.ts, recordStorage.ts, workspaceStorage.worker.ts), exact transfer-link conditions and index limits (workspaceRecords.ts), retention of all document archive references during selected-head publication (workspaceRecordStore.ts, canvasCatalogStore.ts), and cache limits/invalidation behavior (immutableRecords.ts, canvasCatalogStore.ts).

Only the point, pinned source text and seed supply evidence. Imported repository adapters, HTTP handlers, catalog write helpers and UI transaction callers are not supplied; their wiring or guarantees are not asserted. Acknowledgement-before-UI-installation is the stated RecordStorage contract, not verified caller behavior. No blob reclamation implementation is shown. The central tree retains the boundary's major components and service dependencies while shrinking from 148 to 101 lines (31.8%) and from 10,708 to 7,178 characters (33.0%). Five peripheral trees expand resource ownership, MCP scope and write classification, chat visibility, live transport state, and evaluation data dependencies. Edges attach to the relevant concepts rather than arbitrary tree roots. Positions account for actual text dimensions and leave gaps.

The decomposition combines modular structure with call paths, ownership and data dependencies. Evidence comes only from the supplied point, seed and pinned source text. The lifetime tree follows bootstrap.ts and vitePlugin.ts; scope follows apiAccess.ts, agentRoutes.ts and infrastructure/mapping/mcp/server.ts; chat follows agentChatRoutes.ts; live follows liveCanvasRoutes.ts; evaluation follows bootstrap.ts and evalRoutes.ts.

Source-grounded corrections: bootstrap also exposes diffSessionWorkflows and pushIntegrations. Chat projection removes generation.history specifically, not all retained conversation history. Socket binding occurs on attach/publish messages; the implementation does not require the literal first received frame to establish a role. Final diagram-tool validation applies whenever there is no chat binding, including explicitly targeted connections. The comparison generation tool is named generate-diagram-comparisons. The peripherals also show details absent from the seed: fake comparison runtime selection, context source resolution, MCP readOnlyHint versus the narrower HTTP POST allowlist, context-request serialization, weak ETag matching, and evaluation response projections.

Imported service implementations and comparison/push/diff handlers are not supplied. Their internal persistence, authorization and execution guarantees remain unverified. MCP retry guidance is shown as an advertised contract, not proof of service-level idempotency.

Live Canvas Agent Protocol
|-- Tool requests -> AgentDiagrammingSessionService
|   |-- Bind the target
|   |   |-- canvas.list() -> registered browser workspaces and documents
|   |   |-- canvas.attach(canvasId, documentId) -> sessionId + current version
|   |   |   `-- Session retains canvasId, documentId and optional changeSessionId
|   |   `-- callBound(token) captures the chat target and lazily attaches
|   |       `-- Conflicting explicit session -> CHAT_BINDING_MISMATCH
|   |-- Validate before execution
|   |   |-- contracts.ts schemas validate tool arguments and canvas methods
|   |   |-- Read-only access restricts tools and individual exec methods
|   |   `-- Mutations require version guards; context changes also pin revisionId
|   |-- Route by attachment
|   |   |-- Live document -> CanvasSessionPort -> owning browser
|   |   |-- Proposal document -> ChangeSessionService snapshot/apply
|   |   |   |-- Attachment and changeSessionId must match
|   |   |   `-- save_diagram cannot publish proposal revisions
|   |   `-- Diagram generation -> edit/batch services -> bound browser commands
|   `-- Retain request identity
|       |-- Scope: access mode + change session + tool + session + requestId
|       |-- Same key and arguments -> reuse pending/completed promise
|       |-- Same key with different arguments -> REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT
|       `-- Timeout or rejected/oversized reply -> release request cache entry
|           `-- Retry identical requestId; browser outcome may already be committed
|-- exec(code) -> bounded runtime with replayable API steps
|   |-- QuickJsAgentRuntime exposes frozen canvas, nodes and edges APIs
|   |   |-- 32 MiB memory; 512 KiB stack; 30-second deadline
|   |   `-- Interrupt budget; at most 100 API calls; 4 MiB result limits
|   |-- Capture initial document version and record each method/argument signature
|   |   `-- Mutations require expectedVersion to match the initial version
|   |-- Batched mode [default]
|   |   |-- Consecutive mutations -> queued operations + provisional IDs
|   |   |-- Reads, canvas calls and certain metadata writes flush pending edits
|   |   `-- Final flush -> compact mutation receipts + resulting version
|   |-- Immediate mode
|   |   `-- Each mutation -> apply -> advance version -> return projected result
|   `-- Ambiguous transport failure -> retain execution state
|       |-- Retry replays completed step results
|       |-- Resend unacknowledged work with retained IDs and expected version
|       |-- Changed step or batch sequence -> REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT
|       `-- Unacknowledged steps prevent a successful completion response
|-- Command transport -> CanvasSessionBridge -> useAgentCanvasBridge
|   |-- Browser registers ephemeral canvasId, stableWorkspaceId and documents
|   |-- Backend dispatch assigns command ID and queues document-bound payload
|   |   |-- At most 100 pending commands
|   |   `-- Wake browser long poll; idle poll waits up to 15 seconds
|   |-- Browser processes commands sequentially through its current handler
|   |   |-- Retain up to 200 mutation results keyed by command ID
|   |   `-- Encode reply -> POST value/error with command ID
|   |       `-- Rejected reply -> report CANVAS_REPLY_REJECTED to backend
|   |-- Backend matches canvasId + command ID -> resolve/reject waiting dispatch
|   |   `-- After 25 seconds -> CANVAS_TIMEOUT; outcome may be unknown
|   `-- Lifetime
|       |-- Browser refreshes registration after polling; failure retries after 1 second
|       |-- Bridge list() retires registrations untouched for over 35 seconds
|       `-- Page hide/unmount -> unregister; pending commands fail CANVAS_UNAVAILABLE
|-- Reads -> compact data with explicit reference lifetimes
|   |-- currentCanvasRead(level, nodeIds)
|   |   |-- small -> text, structure, complete selected-diagram evidence/mappings,
|   |   |           collapse state, highlights and jumps with active/stale status
|   |   |-- full -> also geometry, other display objects, edges and canvas view
|   |   `-- Current state only; small reads avoid constructing layout and history
|   |-- CanvasReadAliases for canvas.read()
|   |   |-- Immutable per-read aliases -> original IDs
|   |   |-- Bound to canvas + document + optional change session
|   |   |-- 30-minute expiry; retain at most 128 reads and 50,000 IDs per read
|   |   `-- Expired/unknown alias -> STALE_READ; wrong target -> READ_BINDING_MISMATCH
|   `-- CanvasApiProjection for node APIs and live context
|       |-- ASCII/structure in content; diagram metadata omits duplicate content
|       |-- Opaque anchor handles retain full revision/hash-scoped identity
|       |-- Shared tool/socket handle vocabulary; domain state keeps full IDs
|       `-- Handles never reassigned; unknown handle -> STALE_CONTENT_NODE
|           `-- Backend restart requires rereading handles
|-- Live selection channel -> publishLiveCanvasSelections -> LiveCanvasService
|   |-- One protocol-v2 publisher socket per browser workspace
|   |   `-- Observe each visible draft with its own canvasEpoch and sequence
|   |-- observeCanvasSelection samples completed selection state
|   |   |-- Whole-diagram IDs + regions containing rectangle, text and source IDs
|   |   |-- Changed source text/content binding -> region marked stale
|   |   `-- Coalesce controller notifications; unchanged selection emits nothing
|   |-- Publish bounded updates
|   |   |-- First send or reconnect -> current selection.snapshot
|   |   |-- Same epoch -> selection.delta against last transmitted snapshot
|   |   |   `-- baseSequence + upserted regions + removed IDs + changed diagram IDs
|   |   |-- Coalesce pending state; pause drain above 64 KiB socket buffer
|   |   `-- Hidden/removed/replaced draft -> remove old epoch; dispose observer
|   |-- Service owns publisher identity and validates incoming state
|   |   |-- Old sequence in same epoch -> ignore
|   |   |-- Delta requires matching epoch and baseSequence -> otherwise out of sync
|   |   `-- Enforce unique IDs, region/diagram limits and total region-text limit
|   |-- Agent attach(workspaceInstanceId, documentId)
|   |   |-- Requires published selection -> connectionId bound to canvasEpoch
|   |   |-- Initial bound selection -> later deltas fan out to matching connections
|   |   `-- agents.changed reports active binding count to publisher
|   `-- Identity changes invalidate bindings
|       |-- New document epoch -> canvas.replaced
|       |-- Document removal -> canvas.closed
|       |-- Publisher disconnect -> canvas.disconnected
|       `-- Reject pending copy/paste; old connections must rediscover and attach
|-- Live context and scoped agent context
|   |-- context.get -> load browser context -> CanvasApiProjection
|   |   `-- Recheck publisher, epoch and binding after await; reject replaced state
|   |-- agent-context.upload -> AgentContextService with current live binding
|   |-- Diagram edit/batch context resolution uses workspace + document scope
|   `-- diagram-agent-context
|       |-- read -> absent, ready or stale according to source fingerprint
|       `-- prepare/delete -> check document version + diagram revision
|           `-- Retain exact mutation payload for retry -> apply-diagram-context
`-- Live copy/paste commands also use the publisher socket
    |-- diagram.copy -> normalize ASCII -> stage ephemeral text in browser
    |   `-- Requires advertised diagram.copy capability; user chooses paste position
    |-- diagram.paste -> normalize ASCII -> command with stable nodeId,
    |                   documentId, canvasEpoch, expectedVersion and position
    |   `-- Successful reply must match nodeId and expectedVersion + 1
    `-- Receipt scope: workspace + document + epoch + requestId
        |-- Changed arguments -> REQUEST_ID_REUSED
        |-- Pending duplicate -> share promise; completed duplicate -> reuse result
        |-- 25-second timeout -> retry identical arguments with retained command
        `-- Never evict receipts into possible duplicate insertion
            `-- Each operation has a 2,000-receipt cap and 100-pending cap

Evidence comes only from the point definition and embedded sources in context.json, with seed.json as the starting diagram. sessionService.ts supports routing, replay, context mutation and save details; canvasSessionBridge.ts and useAgentCanvasBridge.ts support polling; readAliases.ts, apiProjection.ts and currentCanvasRead.ts support references; liveCanvasService.ts, liveCanvasPublisher.ts and liveCanvasStatus.ts support socket behavior; contracts.ts and execRuntime.ts establish schemas and execution limits.

Qualifications to the seed: shared tool/socket handles are documented intent, but both services default to separate CanvasApiProjection instances; shared injection is not shown. A replaced draft queues an old-epoch removal, but its new snapshot can overwrite that pending removal, so removal delivery is not unconditional. The blanket mutation version requirement is narrowed: node/edge edits are guarded, while createDocument has no expectedVersion and copyDocument makes it optional. The hook's command-ID cache alone does not establish end-to-end request-ID deduplication because dispatch generates fresh command IDs; the browser handler implementation is outside these inputs.

Additional source-grounded details include whole-read eviction before TTL, late socket replies recording outcomes after timeout, selection equality suppressing version-only changes, jump target validation, serialized saves, and successful publication returning displayUpdated:false when browser acknowledgement fails. Imported context storage/compiler and browser receiver internals remain unverified.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the four main responsibility groups while shrinking from 110 to 74 lines (32.7%) and from 8302 to 5245 characters (36.8%). Five peripheral trees expand conversation state, tool boundaries, child isolation, evidence validation, and retry ownership. The decomposition combines modular boundaries, invocation paths, resource lifetimes, and the data dependencies needed to produce revisions. Edges attach to specific concepts using 1-based raw lines. Positions were checked against actual tree dimensions; no trees overlap.

Source-grounded additions include 32 ms delta buffering, background-chat visibility, fixed native tool definitions versus refreshed MCP tools, retained binding tokens, child-relative token accounting, receipt caching before persistence, saved variant scopes, and Pi's restricted tool/resource configuration. These come from the pinned AgentChatService, AgentChatPanel, ChatDiagramTools, MappingChatMcpBinding, GenerationCanvasBridge, DiagramEditService, DiagramBatchService, PiAgentRuntime, PiDiagramEditRuntime, and validation sources inside context.json.

Correction: the seed says generation cleanup always runs. AgentChatService.finishGeneration saves the final child record before entering the sync try/finally (lines 330-336); a rejected save can bypass that cleanup. The child tree makes this boundary explicit. The bridge's normal port contract also does not imply support for every command: canvas-view list returns empty saved views, save acknowledges, and other view operations reject (generationCanvasBridge.ts:78-85). Saving a chat request ID before turn/start suppresses duplicate attempts but does not guarantee native execution.

Only the supplied point, source text, and seed were used as semantic evidence. Imported implementations such as the live canvas adapter, revision-store helpers, generateDiagram, and AgentDiagrammingSessionService are not pinned here. Their internal guarantees and concrete runtime wiring remain unverified; the diagrams show visible calls and contracts rather than inferred internals. Pi is the supplied DiagramGenerator implementation, distinct from Codex chat transport.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the seed's six conceptual branches while shrinking from 104 to 71 lines (31.7%) and from 7,241 to 4,933 characters (31.9%). Five peripheral trees expand validation/conversion, source capture, durable identities, transient ownership, and diagram backing. Modular boundaries identify public operations and private state; call paths show delegation; ownership distinguishes immutable values, durable records and service memory; data dependencies connect descriptors to pinned evidence. Edges attach to the relevant concept lines. Positions leave gaps between measured text bounds.

Evidence is restricted to context.json and seed.json. The value tree comes from agentContext.ts; sources from agentContextSource.ts and fileAgentContextSources.ts; library from savedAgentContext.ts, agentContextLibrary.ts and fileAgentContextRepository.ts; uploads from agentContextService.ts; diagram backing from diagramAgentContext.ts and fileDiagramAgentContextStore.ts.

Corrections and qualifications: Git reuse compares hashes of parsed line data after CRLF/LF splitting, not exact original bytes. The binary check rejects NUL rather than detecting all binary content. Failed pinned-file reads explicitly remove their cached Promise, allowing retry. Snapshot versions in the seed describe capture choices; loading also accepts higher versions without the corresponding features. Library source persistence is conditional on an injected source service. The actual source-file bound is 16 MiB, despite stale 2 MiB comments/error text in fileAgentContextSources.ts.

Added details include selected-path validation limits, tool-result ordering, repeated-reference byte accounting, retry checks before parent reads, publication race handling, scope bypass for saved-ID routing, and the absence of current-revision comparison during diagram loading. Call paths are inferred from supplied implementations, not observed executions. ImmutableRecords internals, blob reclamation and external consumer behavior are not supplied; no guarantees about those are inferred.

canvas.explanation: The central tree preserves the proposal lifecycle while reducing the seed from 105 to 66 lines (37.1%) and from 7107 to 4309 characters (39.4%). Six peripheral trees expand workflow access and lifetime, push intake, evidence identities, concurrency and recovery, persistence, and review. The trees mix modular boundaries, calls, ownership and concrete data requirements; indentation groups concepts, while edges connect central concepts to their details. New source-grounded details include interrupted-run reporting (diffSessionWorkflowService.ts), the oversized default DiffTree fallback and mapping-only updates (diffTree.ts), manifest-token ownership and 16-entry caches (diagramChangeSessionStore.ts and changeSessionRecords.ts), and preview worker cleanup and acceptance retry IDs (ChangeSessionPreview.tsx). Corrections: edits do not invariably leave a session in draft; ChangeSessionService.update can edit, set draft, then validate and set ready in the same call. Acceptance checks session version and live document content/name, not capturedVersion; it passes savedRevisionId to the catalog. Full hunk coverage belongs to complete_diff_session, not the general validateReady gate. Default commit grouping has a single-node fallback when ASCII exceeds 20000 characters. Uncertainty: only the supplied snapshot was used. The point describes atomic catalog publication, but the catalog implementation is absent; the diagram marks that boundary without asserting a verified transaction. Pinned source reads are the supplied tool's documented contract, but the injected source-reader implementation is absent. Imported helpers are not treated as independently verified implementations.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 127 lines / 9,419 characters to 87 lines / 6,420 characters: approximately 32% less by both measures. Six peripheral trees expand input isolation, execution, linked-output ownership, comparison records, experiment coordination and promotion. They mix modular boundaries, calls, ownership and data dependencies; connecting edges indicate conceptual expansion, not execution order. Positions were checked against actual text dimensions, and endpoints use meaningful 1-based lines.

Details added from the supplied source include checkpoint ancestry stripping, prompt-lineage exceptions, comparison input limits, Judgement tombstones, persisted experiment launch receipts, whole-source-canvas dependency traversal during diagram promotion, and placement backfill.

Corrections and qualifications: EvalPromptService versions changes to template bases or explicit parents as well as stage text; metadata-only edits need not create versions. EvalRunService imports legacy roll-ups during initialization, while migrate handles older generated views. AgentContextEvalRuntime's cleanup guarantee is scoped to its protected execution block, rather than the seed's unqualified 'every exit'. Runtime exceptions bypass generateValidated's validation retries. Session context delivery is restricted to diagram-change-proposal by evalRunRequestSchema. GeneratedCanvasCatalog permits records without generation metadata and excludes unfinished generation when that metadata exists.

Evidence is limited to context.json and seed.json. The few-shot schedule is supported by evalWorkflows and preparation checks, but its executor implementation was not supplied. Likewise, history coordination, fallback runtime internals, several validators/materializers and publication storage are represented only through their supplied contracts and call sites; their internal behavior is not independently established.

discovery.summary: The epicenter is the immutable Diagram revision model plus CanvasHistory and MappingDocumentController. Browser editing, agent commands, isolated generation, change proposals, and evaluations converge on these structures. Eleven selected points capture that shared core, its persistence boundary, and its principal consumers.

points.title: Immutable Diagram Model
points.rationale: Diagram combines versioned ASCII content, parsed nodes, source evidence, highlights, and jumps. Revision operations preserve logical node identities while validating edits. This is the fundamental value shared by rendering, agents, history, and storage; parser versions also protect existing node references.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: CanvasHistory separates diagram revision bindings from composition, personal view state, and saved CanvasViews. MappingDocumentController applies version-checked semantic operations and coordinates checkpoints, alternatives, transfers, and navigation. Browser sessions and isolated server-side canvases reuse this boundary.

relationships.label: binds immutable revisions into canvas checkpoints

points.title: Interactive Canvas Editor
points.rationale: MappingPage assembles the workspace and command receivers. CanvasSession publishes committed state through focused stores, while the tldraw runtime owns live geometry and native undo navigation. Settled gestures become controller commands; rendering, selection, and routing derive from the same semantic document.

relationships.label: commits semantic edits and restores checkpoints
submits workspace changes and flushes acknowledged mutations
opens mapped source through repository services

points.title: Durable Canvas Persistence
points.rationale: Persistence separates immutable diagram/checkpoint records from mutable catalogs and workspace manifests. Browser-side change tracking sends record batches rather than complete histories. Server adapters validate versions and retry receipts, write referenced records first, and publish manifests or catalogs afterward.

relationships.label: stores and restores checkpoint graphs and workspace records
persists immutable revisions behind content-addressed references

points.title: HTTP and MCP Boundary
points.rationale: The Vite adapter exposes application services through HTTP, streaming responses, and live sockets. Bootstrap is the concrete composition root. The MCP server translates tool calls into these HTTP endpoints, making this the principal external access boundary rather than a separate implementation of canvas behavior.

relationships.label: dispatches canvas tools and attaches live readers
exposes chat and generation operations
serves source files and definition lookups
exposes workspace batches and canvas publication
exposes proposal workflows and push intake
exposes evaluation and comparison services

points.title: Live Canvas Agent Protocol
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService binds tools to specific canvases and documents, validates requests, and manages retry-safe execution. Commands travel through a polling bridge to the browser; a separate live service distributes selection/context updates over sockets. Compact projections and revision guards keep agent references tied to the correct state.

relationships.label: dispatches bound browser commands and receives live state
redirects scoped reads and mutations into proposal sessions
uploads and resolves scoped agent context

points.title: Agent Chat and Generation
points.rationale: Agent Chat manages persistent conversations, native Codex events, tool bindings, and independent canvas alternatives. Diagram edit and batch services validate generated revisions before application. Codex stdio and Pi runtimes are distinct execution adapters; GenerationCanvasBridge gives child generations isolated controllers using the normal canvas command contract.

relationships.label: invokes canvas tools through bound sessions
creates isolated controllers for generated alternatives
validates and submits generated revision edits
reuses captured conversations and pinned source context

points.title: Reusable Agent Context
points.rationale: AgentContext captures immutable conversation trajectories and source constituents. The library adds durable identities, lineage, grouping, and retry-safe creation; transient uploads remain workspace/document scoped. Diagram-bound contexts and source snapshots make this a shared input boundary for edits, chat alternatives, and evaluations.

relationships.label: captures source ranges from registered corpus bindings
stores shared immutable source blobs
compiles contexts from diagram evidence and revision identity

points.title: Repository Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves an explicit diagram or source binding rather than assuming one repository per project. Corpus providers handle filesystem reads, the repository registry handles Git identities, and optional language services resolve definitions. Browser repository and source panes consume this boundary to connect diagrams back to code.

relationships.label: resolves mappings, evidence, and source bindings
loads registered sources and saved representation bindings

points.title: Repository Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped canvases and Git hunks into isolated proposals, applies the shared controller operations, and retains baseline/proposed history for review. Acceptance checks captured versions before atomic catalog publication. DiffSession workflows and deduplicated push intake feed this same proposal lifecycle.

relationships.label: forks histories and applies shared controller operations
publishes accepted canvases and recovery receipts
uses agent tools during proposal materialization

points.title: Evaluation and Comparison Workflows
points.rationale: Evaluation runs pin prompt versions, contexts, and canvas checkpoints before generation. Materializers turn validated results into canvas outputs; comparison sessions preserve independent input copies. Experiments, judgements, and promotion build on these records, making this a substantial consumer of the shared model rather than a parallel diagram system.

relationships.label: pins and materializes independent canvas histories
loads immutable generation inputs
publishes promoted outputs into project catalogs
reconciles chat-generated alternatives into evaluation records
captures proposal sessions as evaluation outputs

limitations: Review depth varies. reviewedPaths includes files inspected through source declarations, imports, test names/assertions, or other excerpts; it does not mean every file was read in full. Central definitions and callers were traced in greater detail.

Many implementation and test bodies remain uninspected, particularly peripheral UI components, styles, benchmark/browser harnesses, migration scripts, projection-3d, and Python parser experiments. This is a global architectural assessment, not an exhaustive code audit.
The offline static-analysis subsystem and supporting tooling were considered but omitted from the selected epicenter. Their omission does not imply they are unused.

Assessment is limited to the working-tree snapshot captured at 2026-11-11T05:54:36.232538+00:00, based on head 8ca143700ca4d2c870f1101b8cd4601ab68abd41. Index exclusions include corpus, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor, node_modules, most documentation, binary/assets, and lockfiles.

No live repository, external sources, or existing diagram presentation was used to establish the architecture. Tests and runtime integrations were not executed; relationships reflect inspected source.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the value boundary, parsing dependencies, revision flow, edit consumers, and ownership model while shrinking from 103 to 66 lines (35.9%) and from 7206 to 4663 characters (35.3%). Five peripheral trees branch from the concepts they expand. M denotes modular structure, C calls, O ownership, and D data dependency; these perspectives can coexist within a tree. Positions use measured text dimensions with gaps between all diagram rectangles.

All code claims use the pinned sources in context.json. Parser detail comes from diagramContent.ts, diagramContentNodes.ts, asciiTree.ts, asciiGraph/parseAsciiGraph.ts, and interpreter/index.ts. Evidence joins use diagram.ts; identity continuity uses diagramRevision.ts, diagramRevisionEditor.ts, and diagramRevisionStore.ts; scope and connections use diagramSubtreeEdit.ts and diagramConnection.ts. Details absent from the seed include interpreter explanations, frame borders excluding edges, precise subtree gap rules, jump-view projection, and asymmetric connection endpoint types.

Corrections and qualifications: retainMappings is exposed on patches and replace, not single patch. Connection collection validation accepts any differing content revision; it does not establish that the revision is older. The seed's relative-path claim is stronger than validateDiagram's actual guard: it rejects leading '/' and '..' segments but does not reject every absolute-path form. Subtree range calculation uses node anchor lines and root fold ranges, without consulting multiline spans. Durable flush-before-publication is a documented adapter contract, not an implementation shown here. Imported helpers and registry internals absent from the supplied sources remain outside the evidence boundary.

Canvas Commands and History
|-- [M] Shared editing boundary
|   |-- MappingDocumentController: semantic commands + observable canvas snapshot
|   |   |-- Public: applyUpdate/transact, commitEditorGesture, undo/reset, CanvasView commands
|   |   |-- Public: prepare transfers, compare views, export history, read persistence changes
|   |   `-- Private: operation dispatch, staged node correspondence, snapshot/cache/listeners
|   |-- CanvasHistoryService: context-scoped access to history
|   |   |-- Controller depends on this interface; implementation can be injected
|   |   |-- DefaultCanvasHistoryService delegates to CanvasHistory
|   |   `-- Transport callers export records; they must not interpret revision tables
|   |-- CanvasHistory: checkpoints, revision bindings, navigation, named views
|   |   |-- Private record + validation cache + incremental checkpoint encoder
|   |   `-- Depends on diagram revision registry/editor and document validators
|   |-- Composition machinery: GridBox edits -> layout -> projection
|   |   `-- Depends on diagram contents, connections, selections and presentation settings
|   `-- Browser and headless use the same domain history
|       |-- Mounted editor attaches one driver for gesture settlement and native undo
|       `-- Headless proposals retain history without an editor driver
|
|-- [O] Who retains which state
|   |-- Runtime context lifetime
|   |   |-- Service creates CanvasHistory + a frozen CanvasEditingContext handle
|   |   |-- Private WeakMap keys histories by handle identity, not contextId alone
|   |   |   `-- Two viewers of the same saved context remain isolated; handles allow GC
|   |   `-- Runtime handles and service instances are excluded from saved canvases
|   |-- CanvasHistoryRecord owns navigation and retained history
|   |   |-- baselineId + headId + past/future checkpoint IDs
|   |   |-- snapshots: checkpoint ID -> StoredCanvasSnapshot
|   |   `-- diagramRevisions: revision ID -> immutable DiagramRevision
|   |-- Each checkpoint separates four concerns
|   |   |-- diagramBindings: content ID -> exact diagram revision ID
|   |   |-- document: composition and semantic presentation state
|   |   |   |-- GridBox root, canonical edges, sections and jumps
|   |   |   `-- Alternatives, presentations, agent contexts, selections and reviews
|   |   |-- view: personal MappingCanvasState
|   |   |   |-- Camera, selection, per-instance diagram views and floating display state
|   |   |   `-- Controls/surfaces are separate from the display ownership tree
|   |   `-- nodeOrigins + optional unresolved anchors preserve identity/staleness
|   |-- Saved CanvasViews belong to the history header
|   |   |-- Named checkpoint sequences, ancestry, working copies and generation status
|   |   `-- Undo or applying a saved endpoint does not restore this metadata
|   |-- A placement and its diagram have distinct identities
|   |   |-- duplicate-instance creates a new GridBox that shares contentId
|   |   `-- Each instance can retain its own collapsed-subtree view
|   `-- Retention and transport
|       |-- Checkpoints retain bound revisions plus alternative/review/selection dependencies
|       |-- currentOnly export keeps head dependencies and records omitted parent boundaries
|       |-- Saved views or an active recording force full-history export
|       |-- fork creates a new context/baseline, resets navigation, removes active recording

|
|-- [C] Apply a semantic edit
|   |-- API: transact -> applyUpdate -> settle pending editor gesture
|   |   `-- Clear pending node map; call applyOperations; return version + display nodes
|   |-- Native gesture: commitEditorGesture -> applyOperations with gesture canvas state
|   |   `-- Selection-only gesture can directly record the updated canvas state
|   `-- applyOperations(expectedVersion, operations)
|       |-- Reject stale controller version or invalid batch size
|       |-- Clone current document + canvas; run operations in order on staged state
|       |   |-- Diagram content: create, insert, patch, replace, receive a revision
|       |   |   |-- Content edits issue revisions; later operations see earlier staged edits
|       |   |   `-- Track node correspondence; rebase affected anchors, jumps and views

|       |   |   |-- Grid positions use cells; floating positions use pixels

|       |   |-- Meaning/presentation: mappings, contexts, highlights, edges and jumps
|       |   `-- Alternatives/reviews: store, select, review and apply candidate revisions
|       |       `-- Relevant operations also check expected revision, hash or node identity
|       |-- Prune obsolete contexts/alternatives; validate projection; repair active focus
|       `-- updateSnapshot(record = true)
|           |-- Normalize selections and diagram views; reconcile connections/jumps
|           |-- Resolve floating geometry and validate connections
|           |-- historyService.append -> CanvasHistory.append
|           |   |-- Validate document and revision references before publishing checkpoint
|           |   |-- Bind exact revisions, retain dependencies, encode logical edge anchors
|           |   `-- Save document + view; push old head to past; set head; clear future
|           `-- Publish controller snapshot, advance version, notify subscribers
|               |-- One successful command batch/gesture produces one checkpoint

|-- [C] Navigate checkpoints and named alternatives

|   |   |-- Mounted editor -> editor driver -> restore archived semantic checkpoint

|   |   |   `-- Validate target; move IDs between past/future; restore document + view
|   |   `-- Transaction-linked navigation is rejected locally; use workspace transfer undo
|   |-- reset -> append a fresh checkpoint containing the baseline state

|   |   |-- open -> stash departing working copy; resume target working copy or saved end
|   |   |   `-- Create a fresh checkpoint while retaining the current camera

|   |   |-- alternatives -> independent children of ONE pinned saved endpoint
|   |   |   `-- Group creation does not switch the active canvas
|   |   |-- keep -> save chosen child; archive group siblings and their descendants
|   |   |-- discard -> archive target and descendants; delete only permits a leaf
|   |   |-- Legacy recording: start -> collect visited checkpoints -> stop and save
|   |   |   `-- cancel removes recording metadata while keeping edits
|   |   `-- Legacy apply -> fresh checkpoint of saved endpoint, without transfer linkage
|   |-- Generation uses isolated proposals
|   |   |-- startGeneration -> pin parent saved state and register candidate views
|   |   |-- updateGeneration checks candidate run/chat identity and settlement status
|   |   `-- Finished proposal -> validate/import revisions and advance candidate endpoint
|   |       `-- Live head stays in place; opening the candidate is a separate action
|   `-- Comparison and dirty state
|       |-- canvasViewComparison reads only pinned start/final checkpoints
|       |-- promote-diffs adds diagram alternatives while retaining original checkpoints
|       `-- Dirty comparison excludes camera and selection, but includes other view state
|
|-- [C] Transfer diagrams across canvases

|   |   |-- Require distinct canvases and a nonempty, unique selection of diagram boxes
|   |   |-- Preserve relative placement; map box/content identities and rebase annotations
|   |   |-- copy
|   |   |   |-- Allocate fresh box/content identities; leave source history unchanged
|   |   |   `-- Copy only edges whose two endpoints are selected; remap their anchors

The central tree is reduced from 137 to 95 lines (30.7%) and from 11,139 to 7,455 characters (33.1%). It retains modular boundaries and dependencies [M], invocation paths [C], responsibility and lifetime [O], and reconstruction dependencies [D]. Five peripheral trees expand retry state, batch acceptance, checkpoint encoding, publication, and selective reads. Positions use measured text dimensions with horizontal gaps of at least 8 characters and vertical gaps of 6 lines.

Grounding: retry uses workspacePersistence.ts, recordStorage.ts, workspaceStorage.worker.ts and workspaceRecords.ts; commit uses workspaceRecordStore.ts, workspaceRecords.ts, immutableRecords.ts and diagramRevisionStore.ts; codec uses canvasCheckpointRecords.ts and workspaceRecords.ts; publish uses diagramService.ts, projectCatalogRepository.ts, canvasCatalogStore.ts, workspaceRecordStore.ts, diagramPersistence.ts and workspaceService.ts; reads uses diagramPersistence.ts, canvasCatalogStore.ts, workspaceRecordStore.ts and the worker. Added details include the 512-character text threshold, reversible reference diffs, identity-based restoration reuse, exact retry timing, transfer-mode checks, and source-binding cache invalidation.

Corrections and qualifications: loadDiagramSourceBindings passes all catalog revisions' histories, so its scan is not restricted to representations' current published revisions. Workspace publication waits for every writer even on failure, but a writer rejection throws BEFORE blob-directory sync and manifest publication. Capture hydrates only the selected head and bound revisions, but retains references to every checkpoint/revision/item key for that document. Workspace history=current changes validation, not the set of manifest blobs loaded on a cache miss. Queues are module-local per root or instance-local; cross-process locking is not established.

Only the supplied point, seed and pinned source text were used as evidence. HTTP route/transport composition and the writeJsonAtomic implementation are not supplied: the central tree marks the wiring gap, and catalog write ordering is shown without asserting its fsync implementation. DiagramRevisionStore has no explicit fsync; workspace atomic writes and the separate publishJson helper do. No blob reclamation appears in these sources; its absence elsewhere is unknown.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the boundary's major components and contracts while reducing the seed from 147 to 102 lines (30.6%) and from 10,965 to 7,505 characters (31.6%). Six peripheral trees expand composition, MCP scope, HTTP admission, chat streaming, live sockets and evaluation. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] calls, [O] ownership and [D] data dependency; these perspectives can coexist within each tree. Edges attach to the corresponding central concept lines. Positions leave gaps between the measured text bounds.

Only context.json and seed.json supply evidence. Composition details come from bootstrap.ts; MCP details from infrastructure/mapping/mcp/server.ts and scripts/mapping/mcp.ts; admission from vitePlugin.ts, apiAccess.ts, http.ts and agentRoutes.ts; streaming from agentChatRoutes.ts and liveCanvasRoutes.ts; evaluation from evalRoutes.ts and the mapping router.

Corrections and qualifications: the seed's broad public-session/event filtering claim is narrowed to the explicit publicSession/publicEvent paths; list and generations routes delegate directly, so their filtering cannot be inferred here. The socket implementation permits errors before successful attach/publish, rather than enforcing that the first validated frame selects a role. Fake mode switches selected runtimes, while Agent Chat still receives StdioCodexConnection and diff workflows receive PiDiffSessionRuntime. Diagram-tool validation without a chat binding also applies to target-bound connections, so 'unbound' was too ambiguous.

New source-grounded details include context-source resolution, the distinction between MCP readOnlyHint and HTTP gate exemptions, extra MCP callbacks omitting the binding header, precise snapshot shortening, weak/wildcard ETag matching, and evaluation input dependencies. Imported service implementations and schemas are not supplied; delegation does not establish their internal validation, persistence or authorization behavior.

Live Canvas Agent Protocol
|-- [M] Bound tool gateway: AgentDiagrammingSessionService
|   |-- Public entry points: callBound, call, submitDirect
|   |   |-- Contracts define tool schemas and canvas/nodes/edges methods
|   |   `-- Private machinery owns attachment, dispatch, snapshots and retry execution
|   |-- [C] callBound(token, tool, arguments)
|   |   |-- Capture chat target and read-only access
|   |   |-- Lazily attach targeted calls to captured canvas + document
|   |   |   |-- Verify document appears in the canvas descriptor
|   |   |   |-- Read identity; retain sessionId -> canvasId + documentId + optional changeSessionId
|   |   |   `-- Conflicting caller attachment -> CHAT_BINDING_MISMATCH
|   |   `-- Validate arguments -> enforce tool/method permissions -> resolve references -> execute
|   |-- [O] Request history belongs to the service
|   |   |-- Key includes access mode, change session, tool, session and requestId
|   |   |-- Same key + same arguments -> reuse promise
|   |   |-- Same key + changed arguments -> REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT
|   |   |-- Ambiguous transport failure -> remove request promise so identical retry can proceed
|   |   `-- Successful versioned pure exec reads release cached payloads
|   `-- [C] Route according to attachment
|       |-- Live document -> CanvasSessionPort dispatches to owning browser
|       |-- Proposal document -> ChangeSessionService supplies snapshots and applies operations
|       |   `-- Attachment must match changeSessionId; proposal save cannot publish catalog revisions
|       `-- Generated edits/batches -> edit services -> bound browser revision/create/batch commands
|
|-- [M] Script execution boundary: AgentExecRuntime -> QuickJsAgentRuntime
|   |-- Exposes frozen canvas, nodes and edges API groups through an invoke callback
|   |   `-- Session service validates each method and converts mutations to DiagramOperations
|   |-- [C] exec(code, sessionId, requestId, expectedVersion)
|   |   |-- Capture initial document version
|   |   |-- Mutation requires expectedVersion == initial version
|   |   |-- Batched mode: queue consecutive mutations and return provisional IDs
|   |   |   |-- Reads and other barriers flush pending operations
|   |   |   `-- Successful script end flushes remaining operations -> compact mutation receipts
|   |   `-- Immediate mode: apply each mutation -> advance version -> return projected node/edge
|   |-- [O] ExecRun retains ordered steps and batches while an outcome is uncertain
|   |   |-- Each step freezes arguments, generated IDs and execution closure
|   |   |-- Each batch retains operation indices, expectedVersion and result/error
|   |   |-- Retry replays completed API outcomes; resends only unacknowledged work
|   |   |   `-- Stable request IDs and versions survive the retry; changed call sequence is rejected
|   |   `-- Success or non-transport failure removes the run; ambiguity keeps it retryable
|   `-- [O] One QuickJS context per run
|       |-- Limits: 32 MiB memory, 512 KiB stack, 30-second deadline, 100 API calls
|       |-- API and final result JSON each limited to 4 MiB
|       `-- finally -> dispose context, including on failure
|
|-- [M] Browser command transport: CanvasSessionPort -> CanvasSessionBridge
|   |-- Contract: register/list, dispatch/poll/reply, unregister/dispose
|   |-- [C] dispatch(canvasId, command)
|   |   `-- Allocate commandId + pending promise -> enqueue -> wake browser poll
|   |       `-- useAgentCanvasBridge receives commands through HTTP polling
|   |           |-- Invoke supplied browser handle(command) sequentially
|   |           |-- Encode value/error with canvasReply -> POST reply
|   |           |   `-- Rejected reply body -> send compact CANVAS_REPLY_REJECTED error
|   |           `-- Bridge matches canvasId + commandId -> resolve/reject caller
|   |-- [O] Bridge owns descriptors, queues, wake callbacks and pending timers
|   |   |-- Empty poll waits up to 15 seconds; dispatch permits at most 100 pending commands
|   |   |-- No reply after 25 seconds -> remove pending command and report uncertain outcome
|   |   |-- list() retires registrations untouched for more than 35 seconds
|   |   `-- Unregister/dispose -> wake pollers, clear timers, reject pending commands
|   `-- [O] Browser hook owns an ephemeral canvasId, polling loop and reply cache
|       |-- Registers descriptor with stable workspace identity; refreshes registration after polls
|       |-- Caches mutation results by commandId, retaining at most 200
|       |-- Polling failure -> retry loop after 1 second
|       `-- Cleanup -> abort requests, clear retry timer and unregister
|           `-- pagehide also unregisters the ephemeral instance
|
|-- [M] Live selection/context boundary: LiveCanvasService + browser publisher
|   |-- Public protocol v2: publish, attach, selection updates, context, copy/paste, context upload
|   |-- [O] One publisher per workspace instance; owner identity guards updates and replies
|   |   |-- Publisher retains per-document selection snapshots
|   |   `-- Each agent binding pins workspaceInstanceId + documentId + canvasEpoch
|   |-- [C] Browser publishes visible draft sessions
|   |   |-- observeCanvasSelection subscribes to each document controller
|   |   |   `-- Coalesce changes -> sample completed regions and whole-diagram selections
|   |   |-- Publisher ready/reconnected -> send current full snapshots
|   |   |-- Later changes -> send selection.delta against last transmitted snapshot
|   |   |   `-- Backpressure above 64 KiB -> defer drain; pending state coalesces per document
|   |   `-- LiveCanvasService.update -> validate -> store mirror -> notify matching agent bindings
|   |       |-- Old sequence in same epoch -> ignore
|   |       |-- Delta needs matching epoch and baseSequence -> otherwise SELECTION_OUT_OF_SYNC
|   |       `-- Enforce unique/bounded regions and diagram IDs; whole diagrams exclude their regions
|   |-- [D] Selection delta
|   |   |-- Last transmitted regions + next regions -> changed/upserted and removed region IDs
|   |   |-- Previous sequence -> baseSequence
|   |   `-- Changed whole-diagram set -> replacement diagramIds
|   |-- [D] Region text and stale flag
|   |   |-- Selection rectangle + selected IDs + current diagram -> clipboard text
|   |   `-- Captured ASCII or box/content binding differs -> stale region preserving captured text
|   |-- [C] Agent attach -> initial bound selection; context request -> loadContext callback
|   |   |-- Context uses compact projection shared with tool reads
|   |   `-- Recheck publisher/epoch and binding after await -> reject replaced or closed canvas
|   |-- [C] Socket copy/paste commands execute in the owning browser
|   |   |-- Normalize supplied text -> retain command -> publisher forwards to browser receiver
|   |   |-- Copy requires diagram.copy capability; stages ephemeral text for user placement
|   |   |-- Paste carries expectedVersion, position and a fixed generated nodeId
|   |   |   `-- Successful reply must match nodeId and expectedVersion + 1
|   |   `-- [O] Receipts keyed by workspace + document + epoch + requestId
|   |       |-- Changed arguments -> REQUEST_ID_REUSED; completed result -> reuse
|   |       |-- Timeout -> retain command for identical retry
|   |       `-- Never evict receipts; reject new work when history capacity is reached
|   `-- [O] Identity and connection lifecycle
|       |-- Hidden/removed/replaced browser draft -> dispose observer and publish removal
|       |-- Document removal/new epoch/publisher disconnect -> invalidate affected bindings
|       |   `-- Reject pending copy/paste waits and notify agents of closed/replaced/disconnected state
|       |-- Agent attach/detach/invalidation -> publish current connected-agent count
|       `-- Browser publisher cleanup -> unsubscribe, dispose observers, clear timers/maps, close socket
|
|-- [M] Read and reference boundary: compact output, full IDs inside domain state
|   |-- [D] currentCanvasRead(state, level, nodeIds)
|   |   |-- Scene + diagram revisions + presentation state -> diagram text and anchors
|   |   |-- Source mappings + evidence + anchor spans -> source ranges for each content node
|   |   |-- Revision relationships -> active/stale highlights and jumps
|   |   |-- Small: selected diagrams with complete source evidence, without constructing geometry/history
|   |   `-- Full: add geometry, edges and canvas view
|   |-- [O] CanvasReadAliases: immutable tables for canvas.read results
|   |   |-- Each read binds aliases to canvas + document + optional change session
|   |   |-- Arguments resolve only against the same binding
|   |   |-- Expired/missing table -> STALE_READ; wrong binding -> READ_BINDING_MISMATCH
|   |   `-- Retain at most 128 reads, 30-minute TTL; never reassign an alias
|   `-- [O] CanvasApiProjection: revision-scoped content-anchor handles
|       |-- Projects nodes, edges, highlights, jumps and migrations; strips duplicate/internal fields
|       |-- Full revision/hash identity -> opaque handle; reverse table decodes mutation inputs
|       |-- Handles are shared across tool/live reads through the projection instance
|       `-- Never evict/reassign handles; unknown handle -> STALE_CONTENT_NODE and reread
|
`-- [M] Collaborating services beyond the live protocol
    |-- [C] Agent context
    |   |-- Live upload -> AgentContextService.upload with bound canvas/document scope
    |   |-- Edit generation resolves agentContextId within that same scope
    |   `-- Diagram context prepare/delete requires expected document version + diagram revision
    |       `-- Retain prepared mutation payload so retry dispatches the same context
    |-- [C] Search
    |   `-- Bound live snapshot / pinned proposal state / saved catalog revision -> projected results
    `-- [C] Save -> MappingDiagramService
        |-- Serialize saves per live canvas/document
        |-- Whole document: browser checkpoint -> publishCheckpoint -> notify browser saved
        |-- One diagram: version-checked snapshot -> isolate diagram/history -> save
        `-- Publication can succeed even if browser notification fails: displayUpdated = false

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the six conceptual boundaries while shrinking from 10,193 to 6,636 characters (34.9%) and from 138 to 92 lines (33.3%). Five peripheral trees expand retry ownership, selection synchronization, reference identity, connection lifetimes, and persistence. Edges attach to the specific concepts being expanded. Positions use measured text dimensions with non-overlapping gaps. [M] denotes modular structure and exposed/internal boundaries; [C] denotes calls; [O] denotes state/resource ownership; [D] denotes computational data dependencies.

Grounding comes exclusively from the supplied source text and seed. sessionService.ts supports request replay, attachment routing, context preparation, and save sequencing; canvasSessionBridge.ts, useAgentCanvasBridge.ts, and execRuntime.ts support transport and runtime lifetimes. liveCanvasService.ts, liveCanvasPublisher.ts, and liveCanvasStatus.ts support selection dependencies, receipt handling, and identity invalidation. currentCanvasRead.ts, readAliases.ts, apiProjection.ts, and contracts.ts support read representations and reference rules. Peripheral additions include interrupt and capacity limits, alias collection rules, jump-target validation, differing freshness checks, and suppression of documentVersion-only selection updates.

Corrections and qualifications: the seed describes tool/live anchor handles as shared. Contracts document that intention, but both service constructors independently default to new CanvasApiProjection instances; actual sharing requires injection, and composition wiring is absent. The stale-region condition requires captured sourceAscii; a changed binding alone does not establish staleness without it. QuickJS contexts belong to individual runtime invocations, including retries, while ExecRun retains replay state separately. Its deadline is checked through an interrupt callback, not established here as a hard timeout on awaited host work. Browser cleanup explicitly clears active observer/queue maps, rather than every retained map.

The pinned files expose calls into browser handlers, copy/paste receivers, storage, and change-session services without supplying all their implementations. Their internal deduplication, persistence guarantees, and transaction behavior remain unverified; no end-to-end exactly-once or whole-script rollback guarantee is inferred.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the four perspectives while shrinking from 157 to 107 lines (31.8%) and from 11,021 to 7,634 characters (30.7%). Five peripheral trees expand meaningful component, call, ownership and data-dependency nodes. Positions use measured text dimensions with gaps; all edge anchors are 1-based raw lines.

Corrections to the seed: ChatDiagramTools.call submits supplied content through submitDirect; DiagramEditService.generate separately chooses submitStoredDiagramEdit or generator-backed generation. The central tree therefore separates direct chat submission from the general batch workflow instead of implying that direct chat edits invoke Pi. AgentChatService.interrupt is separate from receive, and callBoundTool is a parallel entry into dispatchTool rather than a continuation of native tool handling. GenerationCanvasBridge.dispatch rejects inactive generation-* IDs instead of forwarding every unknown ID to the live port. FakeDiagramEditRuntime is a sibling implementation of DiagramGenerator, not part of PiDiagramEditRuntime.

Added source-grounded detail includes tool catalog refresh and retained tokens (AgentChatService.reloadTools; MappingChatMcpBinding), attachment caching and run ownership (ChatDiagramTools), exact fork boundaries, generation usage baselines and replay inputs (AgentChatService), controller identity and receipt ordering (GenerationCanvasBridge), mapping-policy checks and retained accepted submissions (generatedDiagramEdit.ts; validatedSubmission.ts), application-error classification (DiagramBatchService; DiagramEditService), and event buffering and RPC lifetimes (AgentChatService; StdioCodexConnection).

Only the supplied point, pinned source text and seed were used as evidence. HTTP routing, submitDirect-to-batch wiring, and imported revision/controller/storage implementations are not supplied; their internal behavior is not independently established here. The diagrams show the visible calls and contracts without asserting database transaction guarantees or filesystem isolation for child generations.
