canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains all five conceptual boundaries while shrinking from 120 lines / 8,796 characters to 77 lines / 5,949 characters: 35.8% fewer lines and 32.4% fewer characters. Four peripherals expand validation/model conversion, retry and storage ownership, pinned evidence, and diagram identity. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] calls or execution sequences, [O] ownership/lifetime, and [D] data dependencies; data dependencies remain distinct from organizational boundaries. Edges connect specific concept lines, using 1-based numbering. Positions were checked against actual text dimensions for non-overlap.

Corrections: agentContext.ts establishes that toPiMessages calls agentContextModelContent; resolveSources is a separate caller-managed prerequisite, not the invocation chain suggested by the seed. Recomputing a descriptor hash does not necessarily change it, particularly when portable conversion leaves descriptors identical. diagramAgentContext.ts makes the inline wrapper contentHash optional, requires it for stored references, and does not verify freshness against the current revision or recompute sourceFingerprint during loading.

Additional source-grounded details include validation limited to the selected parent walk, out-of-order matching tool results, repeated-range byte accounting, distinct request/descriptor hashing rules, comment retries preceding current-hash checks, service-wide capacity, Git cache eviction order, and sourceId fallback during diagram capture. fileAgentContextSources.ts enforces the imported 16 MiB limit despite a stale 2 MiB diagnostic/comment.

Evidence is limited to the point definition, nine embedded source files in context.json, and seed.json. The peripherals derive from agentContext.ts, agentContextSource.ts, savedAgentContext.ts, agentContextLibrary.ts, agentContextService.ts, fileAgentContextRepository.ts, fileAgentContextSources.ts, diagramAgentContext.ts, and fileDiagramAgentContextStore.ts. ImmutableRecords internals, crash recovery, garbage collection, and downstream edit/chat/evaluation integration are not established by these inputs; no implementation guarantees beyond the supplied code are assumed.

Five connected peripheral trees expand selection, storage, cache ownership, pane/rendering behavior, and language-session lifetimes. Corrections and qualifications: SourceCodePane.tsx shows that mapped-range reveal bypasses navigate() and leaves history unchanged. corpus.ts permits an empty directory path for the root; it rejects empty segments within nonempty paths. Symlinks can appear in listings as files, although access through them is rejected. sourceFileCache.ts prioritizes pending work without preempting running loads. projectLanguageService.ts owns sessions per service instance, so application-wide singleton sharing is not established.

Added source-grounded details include binding conflict checks omitting revision (diagramSource.ts), EOF clipping and current-filesystem reads regardless of binding.revision (corpus.ts), repository ID derivation and comparisonBase handling (repositoryRegistry.ts), uncancelled cache replacements and absent eviction limits (sourceFileCache.ts), bounded visit history and measured 80-row rendering chunks (SourceCodePane.tsx and SourceCodeView.tsx), and language-server encoding negotiation and process cleanup (projectLanguageService.ts).

Only context.json and seed.json supplied evidence. canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the workflow overview while shrinking from 163 to 108 lines (33.7%) and from 11,792 to 7,991 characters (32.2%). Six peripheral trees expand evidence capture, execution lifetime, bundle construction, comparison, experiments and promotion. [M] denotes modular structure and exposed/internal boundaries, [C] calls, [O] ownership and lifetime, and [D] data dependencies. Connections anchor to the corresponding central concepts. Positions account for measured text dimensions, with at least 12 columns between occupied diagram bounds.

Source-grounded corrections and qualifications: JudgementService.reconcile is private, invoked by public list/read, rather than an exposed entry point (judgementService.ts:26,101-114). Session context delivery is restricted to diagram-change-proposal (evalRun.ts:26-28). Prompt versions can advance for template-base changes or explicit parents even when stage text is unchanged (evalPromptService.ts:161-164). Deletion scope differs: deleteRun includes reruns, while deleteRuns preserves unselected reruns (evalRunService.ts:742-750). Promotion traverses all jumps on included canvases even when selecting one diagram; targets outside the retained result remain unchanged, so the seed's link-remapping assurance must be limited to bundle dependencies (outputPromotion.ts:49-79). Generated comparison rejects matching document/view identities even across different checkpoints, while manual sessions support self-comparison (comparisonGenerationService.ts:112-118; compareSessionService.ts:184-197).

Additional source details include revision-parent boundaries in endpoint copies, comparison size limits and restart recovery, private experiment launch receipts, and placement backfill restrictions. Evidence is limited to context.json's pinned sources and seed.json. External runner, delegated runtime, few-shot executor and storage implementations are not supplied; their internals are not inferred. The few-shot quantities describe the supplied workflow contract, and retained or frozen evidence means captured records/clones, not a demonstrated runtime immutability mechanism.

discovery.summary: The codebase is a diagram authoring and experimentation system built around immutable diagram revisions and revision-bound canvas composition. Browser editing, agent tools, generated alternatives, and Git change proposals converge on shared canvas commands and history. Persistence, source evidence, reusable agent contexts, and evaluation workflows form the main supporting boundaries; static architecture analysis is a separate tooling subsystem.

points.title: Runtime Composition and APIs
points.rationale: The backend composition root connects application services to filesystem stores, model runtimes, browser bridges, and language services. Its Vite adapter exposes the core and mapping APIs, translates errors, controls optional capabilities, and owns shutdown. This is the strongest anchor for understanding deployment and dependency wiring.

relationships.label: Constructs and injects durable repositories
Wires canvas services and WebSocket transport
Constructs chat runtime and tool bindings
Connects push ingestion to proposal workflows
Assembles evaluation services and generation reconciliation

points.title: Immutable Diagram Revisions
points.rationale: Diagram identity, parsed ASCII content, logical node continuity, source mappings, and revision ancestry meet here. Creation and editing issue validated immutable revisions; the runtime registry preserves their identity. This separates diagram content from its placements and provides the shared foundation for editing, generation, comparison, and persistence.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: MappingDocumentController is the shared semantic mutation boundary for browser edits and isolated proposals. It validates versions and operation batches, coordinates placements and connections, and delegates checkpoints, named views, branching, and undo history to CanvasHistoryService. Canvas checkpoints bind exact diagram revisions independently of composition and personal view state.

relationships.label: Binds and revises immutable diagram content
Produces incremental checkpoint records
Retains diagram context bindings in checkpoints

points.title: Interactive Canvas Runtime
points.rationale: CanvasWorkspace owns document-session lifetimes, while CanvasSession exposes separate reactive stores for document, presentation, selection, controls, and status. The tldraw adapter owns live geometry and native undo navigation, committing settled gestures through the domain controller. Shape projection and routing connect semantic diagrams to interactive rendering without persisting every pointer frame.

relationships.label: Owns controllers and commits settled gestures
Submits workspace changes and publication requests
Registers browser canvases and handles dispatched commands
Hosts chat with the active canvas context

points.title: Checkpoint and Catalog Persistence
points.rationale: Persistence separates immutable content and checkpoint records from mutable manifests and published catalog entries. Browser changes become incremental record batches with version checks and retry identities; server stores publish references after backing records exist. This boundary supports durable history, efficient current-state reads, publication, and atomic acceptance of multi-canvas changes.

relationships.label: Stores and restores validated immutable revisions
Serializes checkpoint graphs and exact revision bindings

points.title: Source Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves a diagram's explicit repository binding instead of assuming one repository per project. Mapped nodes resolve to source ranges, corpus providers supply bounded repository-relative access, and optional language-service sessions resolve definitions against verified source hashes. These constructs connect visual diagrams to inspectable backing code.

relationships.label: Resolves node mappings and diagram source evidence
Loads published source bindings and revisions

points.title: Live Canvas Agent API
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService exposes canvas reads and mutations through HTTP-backed MCP tools and a constrained JavaScript execution runtime. A command bridge reaches the owning browser, while LiveCanvasService maintains separately bound selection streams. Compact anchor projection, version checks, and retry receipts preserve identity across these transport boundaries.

relationships.label: Dispatches live commands to the owning browser
Uses shared semantic commands and current-state projections
Starts and monitors diagram edit batches
Routes proposal-scoped reads and mutations
Exposes saved and diagram-bound context operations

points.title: Reusable Agent Contexts
points.rationale: AgentContext models a validated, hash-addressed conversation and source-evidence snapshot that can seed independent model sessions. The library adds durable discovery, forks, comments, and lineage; source adapters retain exact Git content or immutable snapshots. Diagram-bound contexts reuse this machinery while detecting changes to their captured evidence.

relationships.label: Compiles reusable context from diagram evidence
Captures and resolves repository source ranges
Uses immutable records for captured source content

points.title: Validated Diagram Generation
points.rationale: DiagramEditService and DiagramBatchService coordinate asynchronous creation, extension, scoped replacement, and alternatives against pinned input revisions. Model execution remains behind generator ports; validated submission and domain revision issuance precede application. Runs distinguish generation from application acknowledgement so ambiguous retries do not regenerate or duplicate edits.

relationships.label: Validates generated edits and issues revisions
Seeds generation with captured context
Applies prepared revisions through versioned canvas ports

points.title: Agent Chat Orchestration
points.rationale: AgentChatService manages persisted conversations, native thread resume, streaming events, turn-bound tools, and alternative generation through a Codex app-server connection. GenerationCanvasBridge supplies each candidate with an isolated controller behind the same canvas port. This makes chat both an interactive client of canvas tools and a coordinator of independent generated alternatives.

relationships.label: Invokes tools bound to the current chat turn
Owns isolated controllers for generated alternatives
Loads saved contexts for independent child conversations
Generated alternatives are reconciled into evaluation runs

points.title: Git Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped canvas baselines and Git hunks, edits isolated proposals, derives review changes, and accepts ready proposals only against unchanged originals. A two-stage agent workflow analyzes and materializes proposals; push ingestion resolves pinned commit endpoints and deduplicates external events before starting that workflow.

relationships.label: Edits isolated proposals with shared controllers
Persists proposal records and atomically publishes acceptance
Uses canvas tools during proposal materialization
Runs validated sequential agent workflow steps

points.title: Generation Evaluation Workbench
points.rationale: Evaluation runs pin prompts, contexts, canvas inputs, and output provenance across workflows and repeated samples. Comparisons capture independent snapshots; experiments organize conditions and attempts; judgements preserve typed assessments. Completed outputs can be promoted through the same catalog publication boundary, making this a substantial product subsystem rather than test infrastructure.

relationships.label: Pins and resolves shared evaluation inputs
Reuses persisted agent-session execution
Reads checkpoint records and publishes promoted outputs
Captures proposal results as evaluation outputs
Preserves exact canvas histories for comparisons

points.title: Static Architecture Analysis
points.rationale: A separate TypeScript analysis pipeline extracts containment, lexical references, calls, ownership, and dependencies with explicit evidence provenance. It supports incremental reuse, partition metrics, deterministic artifacts, and joins from pinned diagram leaf ranges to source entities. The inspected CLI invokes it independently of the interactive backend.

relationships.label: Defines joins from pinned diagram leaves to source entities

limitations: The requested complete source read was not achieved. All 1,044 inventory entries received a source-level survey using declarations, test descriptions, or short excerpts; reviewedPaths lists the files examined beyond that survey. Several large listed files were inspected selectively rather than in full.

Most test bodies, peripheral UI components and styles, benchmark implementations, migration scripts, the standalone projection-3d prototype, and Python parser tooling did not receive detailed implementation review. Parser and static-analysis internals were only partially inspected.
The index excludes corpus data, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor dependencies, node_modules, documentation other than the root README, binary/assets, and lockfiles.
Relationships describe inspected static wiring and call paths. No application, tests, model runtimes, or external integrations were executed; no live repository or external sources were consulted.

canvas.explanation: The central tree retains the deployment, composition, API and shutdown spine while reducing the seed from 10,402 to 7,197 characters (30.8%) and from 150 to 101 lines (32.7%). Six peripheral trees expand meaningful concept nodes using modular boundaries, invocation flow, resource ownership and data dependencies. Positions use measured text bounds with gaps; all edge anchors are 1-based raw lines. Evidence is limited to the supplied point, seed and six pinned source texts. Configuration comes from vite.config.ts and vitePlugin.ts; shared state and evaluation wiring from bootstrap.ts; request details from the two routes.ts files; boundary assertions from dependencies.test.ts. The seed's blanket core-method 405 statement is qualified: corpus-compactions calls requireProject before selecting a method, so validation can fail first. Socket capabilities are described as passed options because their enforcement implementation is absent. Additional source-grounded details include runtimes unaffected by fake selection, DELETE diagrams/publish reaching the generic ID route, optional-service fallthrough, callback arguments, and import-test coverage limits. Shutdown interruption on a synchronous throw follows from the unguarded sequential dispose calls. Constructor edges establish injection, not unshown internal behavior. Delegated handlers, mutation classification, header authentication, service outcomes and source classification internals are not supplied; no claims about those implementations or architecture-test success are made.

canvas.explanation: The central tree retains the seed's seven conceptual branches while shrinking from 102 to 67 lines (34.3%) and from 6,858 to 4,752 characters (30.7%). Four peripherals expand parsing, logical identity and read isolation, scoped generation, and source-context dependencies. The decomposition mixes modular boundaries, call paths, ownership, and data dependencies without organizing the trees around files. Peripheral details absent from the seed include sourceId derivation, candidate-claim precedence, view field removal, and the distinction between stored tree nodes and cached diagram nodes. Source-grounded clarification: submitDiagramEdit.ts computes outside/inside mapping combinations for every scoped edit; diagramRevisionEditor.ts uses those supplied mappings only when retainMappings is false, otherwise selecting retainSourceMappings. The durable-flush statement is qualified as an adapter contract documented in diagramRevisionStore.ts, not an implementation demonstrated by these inputs. Mapping and annotation edits can issue new service revisions while preserving content and numeric revision. Evidence validation checks captured strings and their count, not their agreement with repository files. All claims use only the supplied point, seed, and pinned source text. Imported parser, patch, mapping-retention, registry, and durable-adapter internals were not supplied, so their internal behavior is not inferred. Coordinates were checked against actual text dimensions; edges use 1-based concept lines.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains all seven major branches while shrinking from 115 to 76 lines (33.9%) and from 7,755 to 5,262 characters (32.1%). Six peripherals expand meaningful concept nodes using modular boundaries, call paths, state ownership and data dependencies. Positions use measured text dimensions with clear gaps and no overlap; edge line numbers are 1-based.

Source-grounded corrections and qualifications: MappingDocumentController.commitEditorGesture accepts an empty operation list through a direct recorded canvas update; the 1-operation minimum applies to applyOperations (mappingDocumentController.ts:280-286). Opening an already-active CanvasView only stashes its state; switching views prefers a working-copy endpoint over the saved endpoint (canvasHistory.ts:274-288). Move transfer converts EVERY source edge into a jump, including edges between unmoved diagrams, and strictly validates every endpoint (canvasTransfer.ts:134-159). Unrecorded canvas updates leave history unchanged, but select explicitly requests recording (mappingDocumentController.ts:248-253).

Additional detail absent from the seed includes patch propagation into jump spans, collapsed node selections and sections (mappingDocumentController.ts:437-470); collapsed geometry and hit testing (lineGrid.ts:57-95,191-208); endpoint encoding/decoding (canvasHistory.ts:598-631); change-log sequence semantics (canvasHistory.ts:129-135,250-254); and generation identity, count and lifecycle guards (canvasHistory.ts:298-359). History handle isolation is established by canvasHistoryService.ts:49-62; endpoint reconciliation by diagramConnection.ts:47-90.

Evidence is limited to the supplied point, embedded source text and seed. Calls into unprovided helpers are shown only at their visible boundaries. Workspace publication is stated by the transfer source comment; its implementation and runtime behavior were not supplied or tested.

|   |   `-- checkpointHead = head ID + complete reference map for direct reads
|   `-- workspaceRecords.ts -> workspace index + document/<encoded ID>/ records
|       |-- Mutable: metadata, baseline, canvas view, viewport, history header

|       |   |-- Acknowledged -> advance revision and persisted sequence
|       |   `-- Failed -> retain identical batch and request ID

|       |       `-- REJECTED / VERSION_CONFLICT / REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT stop scheduling
|       `-- Explicit commit: flush earlier writes -> submit -> await acknowledgement
|           |-- REJECTED -> restore prior cache and discard abandoned operation
|           `-- Ambiguous failure -> retry same request before allowing another write

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the six main conceptual branches while shrinking from 97 to 65 lines and from 7,083 to 4,713 characters: approximately 33% less content by both measures. Five peripherals expand encoding, browser ownership/retries, workspace acceptance, catalog publication, and read dependencies. Modular boundaries organize the trees; call sequences, state ownership and data dependencies appear within them. Connections attach to the relevant central component or operation. Positions use measured text dimensions with gaps and no overlap.

All detail comes from the supplied source texts. The codec peripheral uses canvasCheckpointRecords.ts and workspaceRecords.ts; browser behavior uses workspacePersistence.ts and recordStorage.ts; workspace acceptance uses workspaceRecordStore.ts and workspaceRecords.ts; catalog behavior uses canvasCatalogStore.ts and diagramRevisionStore.ts; read/cache behavior additionally uses diagramPersistence.ts and immutableRecords.ts. Added details include normalization of interrupted UI operations, cursor/subscription lifetimes, reverse diffs, transfer-mode-specific checks, cache identity requirements and eviction order.

Corrections and qualifications: loadCanvasCheckpoint() with a supplied head map bypasses base-chain/diff validation; it checks loaded item hashes but does not compare that map with the checkpoint's diff. The seed's blanket validation claim is therefore narrowed. Automatic scheduling stops for conflict/rejection errors, but commit() separately retries every non-REJECTED error, including conflicts. Workspace serialization is an in-process queue per root; catalog serialization is per instance. publishCheckpoint() invokes an injected capture callback, rather than directly calling WorkspaceRecordStore.capture(); their wiring is absent. Catalog publication is described by the source as atomic, but the imported writeJsonAtomic implementation is not supplied, so its durability details cannot be verified. DiagramRevisionStore has no explicit fsync, unlike workspace publication and publishJson(). Imported validators and stateKey are shown as dependencies; their internal semantics are not inferred.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 83 to 56 lines (32.5%) and from 5,998 to 3,826 characters (36.2%). Six peripherals expand validation, evidence lifetime, request receipts/lineage, record ownership, model conversion and diagram identity. The center groups responsibilities rather than files; public operations and private state show modular boundaries, call sequences show control flow, and hashes/references show data dependencies. Calls describe supplied code, not observed runtime traces. Edges attach to relevant concept lines. Measured diagram bounds do not overlap.

Corrections: the seed's 'bytes exactly match HEAD' is too strong. fileAgentContextSources.ts:28-31,60-67 splits CRLF/LF before comparing sourceFileHash values, so reuse compares parsed content. The seed's version rules describe newly generated contexts; agentContext.ts:131-148 also accepts version 2/3 without ranges or sections when other validation succeeds. Branch cycle/missing-entry checks stop at fromEntryId rather than checking all ancestry (agentContext.ts:99-121). Diagram fingerprint generation is present, but automatic freshness comparison is not shown (diagramAgentContext.ts:28-30,63-85). The source adapter's '2 MiB' error/comment conflicts with its imported 16 MiB constant; diagrams follow the executable check.

Details beyond the seed include receipt checks before recapture/parent lookup, cache eviction and lifetime, code-unit chunking, per-occurrence expanded byte accounting, sourceId fallback, and full-record reads behind summaries. Evidence is limited to context.json's six pinned sources and point definition plus seed.json. Imported source-range/hash helpers, ImmutableRecords internals, store wiring and session launch callers were not supplied, so their implementations and end-to-end behavior are not asserted.

The central tree retains the generation-to-application flow while shrinking the seed from 102 to 68 lines (33.3%) and from 7,245 to 5,107 characters (29.5%). Five peripheral trees expand pinned inputs, runtime ownership, variant scope, installation retries, and batch preparation. Modular boundaries describe exposed ports and private state; call sequences describe execution; ownership describes retained outputs and sessions; data dependencies explain what each computation requires. Edges attach to the corresponding central concepts using 1-based lines. Positions account for measured text dimensions and leave gaps.

Only context.json and seed.json supplied substantive evidence. Source-grounded qualifications correct overstatements in the seed: diagramEditService.ts passes both versions to apply, but controller enforcement appears only in a comment because its implementation is absent. Retries reuse prepared output within retained service runs; only create explicitly declares requestId idempotency, so duplicate prevention for apply/batch and restart recovery cannot be established here. validatedSubmission.ts asks for correction after rejection and returns a termination flag after acceptance; it does not establish that the model necessarily corrects its output or how the external executor interprets that flag.

Peripheral details absent from the seed include the saved-context session-check exemption and excerpt fallback in diagramEditService.ts; resetting review decisions and selecting only the first requested presentation alternative; explicit-origin reuse across creations; retained maps surviving dispose; model-runtime caching and persisted-message seeding in agentRuntime.ts; accepted submissions surviving a later rejection in validatedSubmission.ts; and provisional child receipts, automatic placement offsets, and indexed errors in diagramBatchService.ts. The supplied files show calls into domain validation/revision publication, but their internal implementations and live canvas mutation semantics are outside the evidence.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the full proposal lifecycle while shrinking from 119 to 79 lines (33.6%) and from 7,992 to 5,338 characters (33.2%). Five peripheral trees expand push ingestion, workflow resources, change derivation, acceptance, and storage. Modular boundaries appear as public services and private machinery; call sequences explain execution; ownership explains histories, promises, receipts and payloads; data dependencies connect captured inputs to computed review results. Authored change.dependsOn relationships are distinguished from computation dependencies.

All details come from the supplied point definition and six embedded source files. Peripheral additions absent from the seed include enabled-check ordering on push replay, workflow map lifetimes, canonical history ownership, four-at-a-time preview loading, bounded caches, and exact hunk-context checks.

Source-grounded corrections: ChangeSessionService.validateReady permits a new or replaced edge source owner when its containing diagram existed in the baseline; it does not require that owner itself to have existed. readTreemaps can fall back to get(), so avoiding full histories and receipts is not unconditional. update can capture hunks when an existing session lacks a DiffTree. Annotation replacement is optional, although any supplied replacement must cover every generated change. Acceptance checks live document content and name, rather than capturedVersion.

The catalog publication implementation, workflow factory, tool implementation and persistence helpers are outside the supplied source. Their internal atomicity, tool permissions and execution guarantees are therefore not expanded beyond the visible calls and checks. Positions use measured text dimensions with horizontal and vertical gaps; edge references use 1-based raw lines.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains all seven major responsibilities while shrinking from 6,334 to 4,294 characters (32.2%) and from 94 to 62 lines (34.0%). Six peripherals expand input contracts, execution, state ownership, experiments, comparison evidence and publication. Modular boundaries identify public operations and private state; call sequences show execution; ownership describes retained records and resource lifetimes; data dependencies connect pinned inputs to outputs and assessments. Edges attach to the relevant concept lines. Positions use measured text dimensions, with at least eight columns between diagram columns and four blank rows between stacked trees.

Corrections and qualifications from the pinned sources: evalPromptService.ts:131-165 appends a version when stages/template base change or explicit parents are supplied; name/description-only edits retain versions. evalRunService.ts:654-668 retries validation failures, while runtime.generate errors propagate. compareSessionService.ts:96-124 permits retained generated checkpoints even when they are not the current workspace head; copyCompareHistory preserves an endpoint and rendering dependencies, not the undo archive. evalRunService.ts:327-337 marks diagram-history cells cancelled without calling an external coordinator abort operation, so cancellation is not universally an execution abort. AgentContextEvalRuntime's cleanup is in its generation try/finally; the seed's claim of disposal on every exit is broader than that protected scope.

Details added beyond the seed include prompt merge constraints and cross-workflow lineage, prompt catalog snapshots, context ownership for canvas-only workflows, private experiment launch receipts, comparison deduplication and revision boundaries, deletion scope differences, and historical placement backfill. These come from the supplied EvalPromptService, EvalRunService, ExperimentService, CompareSessionService, JudgementService and evalRun domain definitions. EvalsPage supports the retained product surface. Imported runtime, materializer, catalog and external coordinator implementations were not supplied; their internal behavior is not inferred. prepareForReview avoids model execution but can create an owning context or a template during preparation.

The central tree is reduced from 104 to 69 lines (33.7%) and from 7,802 to 5,053 characters (35.2%). Five peripheral trees expand modular boundaries, compiler/evidence lifetimes, incremental reuse, dependency graph analysis, and pinned diagram joins. Each connects to its corresponding central concept. Positions use measured text dimensions with gaps between all diagrams.

Containment and lexical scope are combined conceptually as modular structure, while accurately retaining the implementation's five stored views. Ownership is explored through compiler state and checkpoint lifetimes. Dependency graphs remain distinct from the partitions used to organize their entities. Calls describe static evidence; the supplied schema reserves runtime identities but does not establish observed activation traces.

Source-grounded corrections: schema.ts names the lexical relations scope-parent and declares, replacing the seed's scopes and declarations. incremental.ts retains prior dependency edges when both endpoints remain local; it does not establish that those edges are still valid. derive.ts limits the single-group partition to the filtered eligible universe, despite its 'All source entities' label.

Details absent from the seed include caller-specific external summaries, constructor parameter-to-field flow, optional exported metadata that the supplied declaration indexing does not populate, cloned checkpoint boundaries, metrics being absent from fragment cache keys, removedFiles meaning removal from selection, SCC exclusion of isolated entities, and duplicate concept-partition checks. These come from the pinned declarations.ts, context.ts, incremental.ts, derive.ts, schema.ts and sourceJoins.ts.

Uncertainty is retained: imported extractor, metric, persistence and findings helpers whose bodies are not supplied are represented only through visible calls or schema contracts. Coverage marked complete is persisted-site accounting, not proof of exhaustive analysis. No runtime behavior or complete export-visibility map is inferred.

discovery.summary: The codebase is a diagram authoring and experimentation system built around immutable diagram revisions and revision-bound canvas composition. Browser editing, agent tools, generated alternatives, and Git change proposals converge on shared canvas commands and history. Persistence, source evidence, reusable agent contexts, and evaluation workflows form the main supporting boundaries; static architecture analysis is a separate tooling subsystem.

points.title: Runtime Composition and APIs
points.rationale: The backend composition root connects application services to filesystem stores, model runtimes, browser bridges, and language services. Its Vite adapter exposes the core and mapping APIs, translates errors, controls optional capabilities, and owns shutdown. This is the strongest anchor for understanding deployment and dependency wiring.

relationships.label: Constructs and injects durable repositories
Wires canvas services and WebSocket transport
Constructs chat runtime and tool bindings
Connects push ingestion to proposal workflows
Assembles evaluation services and generation reconciliation

points.title: Immutable Diagram Revisions
points.rationale: Diagram identity, parsed ASCII content, logical node continuity, source mappings, and revision ancestry meet here. Creation and editing issue validated immutable revisions; the runtime registry preserves their identity. This separates diagram content from its placements and provides the shared foundation for editing, generation, comparison, and persistence.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: MappingDocumentController is the shared semantic mutation boundary for browser edits and isolated proposals. It validates versions and operation batches, coordinates placements and connections, and delegates checkpoints, named views, branching, and undo history to CanvasHistoryService. Canvas checkpoints bind exact diagram revisions independently of composition and personal view state.

relationships.label: Binds and revises immutable diagram content
Produces incremental checkpoint records
Retains diagram context bindings in checkpoints

points.title: Interactive Canvas Runtime
points.rationale: CanvasWorkspace owns document-session lifetimes, while CanvasSession exposes separate reactive stores for document, presentation, selection, controls, and status. The tldraw adapter owns live geometry and native undo navigation, committing settled gestures through the domain controller. Shape projection and routing connect semantic diagrams to interactive rendering without persisting every pointer frame.

relationships.label: Owns controllers and commits settled gestures
Submits workspace changes and publication requests
Registers browser canvases and handles dispatched commands
Hosts chat with the active canvas context

points.title: Checkpoint and Catalog Persistence
points.rationale: Persistence separates immutable content and checkpoint records from mutable manifests and published catalog entries. Browser changes become incremental record batches with version checks and retry identities; server stores publish references after backing records exist. This boundary supports durable history, efficient current-state reads, publication, and atomic acceptance of multi-canvas changes.

relationships.label: Stores and restores validated immutable revisions
Serializes checkpoint graphs and exact revision bindings

points.title: Source Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves a diagram's explicit repository binding instead of assuming one repository per project. Mapped nodes resolve to source ranges, corpus providers supply bounded repository-relative access, and optional language-service sessions resolve definitions against verified source hashes. These constructs connect visual diagrams to inspectable backing code.

relationships.label: Resolves node mappings and diagram source evidence
Loads published source bindings and revisions

points.title: Live Canvas Agent API
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService exposes canvas reads and mutations through HTTP-backed MCP tools and a constrained JavaScript execution runtime. A command bridge reaches the owning browser, while LiveCanvasService maintains separately bound selection streams. Compact anchor projection, version checks, and retry receipts preserve identity across these transport boundaries.

relationships.label: Dispatches live commands to the owning browser
Uses shared semantic commands and current-state projections
Starts and monitors diagram edit batches
Routes proposal-scoped reads and mutations
Exposes saved and diagram-bound context operations

points.title: Reusable Agent Contexts
points.rationale: AgentContext models a validated, hash-addressed conversation and source-evidence snapshot that can seed independent model sessions. The library adds durable discovery, forks, comments, and lineage; source adapters retain exact Git content or immutable snapshots. Diagram-bound contexts reuse this machinery while detecting changes to their captured evidence.

relationships.label: Compiles reusable context from diagram evidence
Captures and resolves repository source ranges
Uses immutable records for captured source content

points.title: Validated Diagram Generation
points.rationale: DiagramEditService and DiagramBatchService coordinate asynchronous creation, extension, scoped replacement, and alternatives against pinned input revisions. Model execution remains behind generator ports; validated submission and domain revision issuance precede application. Runs distinguish generation from application acknowledgement so ambiguous retries do not regenerate or duplicate edits.

relationships.label: Validates generated edits and issues revisions
Seeds generation with captured context
Applies prepared revisions through versioned canvas ports

points.title: Agent Chat Orchestration
points.rationale: AgentChatService manages persisted conversations, native thread resume, streaming events, turn-bound tools, and alternative generation through a Codex app-server connection. GenerationCanvasBridge supplies each candidate with an isolated controller behind the same canvas port. This makes chat both an interactive client of canvas tools and a coordinator of independent generated alternatives.

relationships.label: Invokes tools bound to the current chat turn
Owns isolated controllers for generated alternatives
Loads saved contexts for independent child conversations
Generated alternatives are reconciled into evaluation runs

points.title: Git Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped canvas baselines and Git hunks, edits isolated proposals, derives review changes, and accepts ready proposals only against unchanged originals. A two-stage agent workflow analyzes and materializes proposals; push ingestion resolves pinned commit endpoints and deduplicates external events before starting that workflow.

relationships.label: Edits isolated proposals with shared controllers
Persists proposal records and atomically publishes acceptance
Uses canvas tools during proposal materialization
Runs validated sequential agent workflow steps

points.title: Generation Evaluation Workbench
points.rationale: Evaluation runs pin prompts, contexts, canvas inputs, and output provenance across workflows and repeated samples. Comparisons capture independent snapshots; experiments organize conditions and attempts; judgements preserve typed assessments. Completed outputs can be promoted through the same catalog publication boundary, making this a substantial product subsystem rather than test infrastructure.

relationships.label: Pins and resolves shared evaluation inputs
Reuses persisted agent-session execution
Reads checkpoint records and publishes promoted outputs
Captures proposal results as evaluation outputs
Preserves exact canvas histories for comparisons

points.title: Static Architecture Analysis
points.rationale: A separate TypeScript analysis pipeline extracts containment, lexical references, calls, ownership, and dependencies with explicit evidence provenance. It supports incremental reuse, partition metrics, deterministic artifacts, and joins from pinned diagram leaf ranges to source entities. The inspected CLI invokes it independently of the interactive backend.

relationships.label: Defines joins from pinned diagram leaves to source entities

limitations: The requested complete source read was not achieved. All 1,044 inventory entries received a source-level survey using declarations, test descriptions, or short excerpts; reviewedPaths lists the files examined beyond that survey. Several large listed files were inspected selectively rather than in full.

Most test bodies, peripheral UI components and styles, benchmark implementations, migration scripts, the standalone projection-3d prototype, and Python parser tooling did not receive detailed implementation review. Parser and static-analysis internals were only partially inspected.
The index excludes corpus data, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor dependencies, node_modules, documentation other than the root README, binary/assets, and lockfiles.
Relationships describe inspected static wiring and call paths. No application, tests, model runtimes, or external integrations were executed; no live repository or external sources were consulted.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the composition boundary, startup, shared service graph, dispatch and shutdown, reduced from 157 to 105 lines (33.1%) and from 10,777 to 7,026 characters (34.8%). Five peripheral trees expand meaningful concept lines. M = modular structure, C = calls, O = ownership/lifetime, D = data dependency; dependencies cross these organizational views. Positions leave gaps calculated from actual tree dimensions.

Evidence is limited to the point definition, seed and six source texts in context.json. Dependency rules come from tests/architecture/dependencies.test.ts; configuration from vite.config.ts; construction, source resolution and evaluation callbacks from src/server/app/bootstrap.ts; transport and lifetime from src/server/app/vitePlugin.ts; endpoint details from the supplied core and mapping routes.ts files.

Source-grounded refinements: the seed's 'no header' condition is a falsy-header check, and the HTTP gate applies only to requests classified as agent mutations. Shutdown registration requires an httpServer. Additional details absent from the seed include static-test exclusions, configuration defaults, named JSON collections, request ordering and publish-route fallthrough: if admitted by the adapter, DELETE /api/mapping/diagrams/publish calls diagrams.delete('publish'). This describes dispatch, not whether that service call succeeds.

The supplied code shows wiring and conditional calls, not observed execution. Implementations of imported handlers, mutation classification, source classification and disposal methods are absent; their internal behavior, authentication guarantees and cleanup completeness cannot be established here.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 102 to 68 lines (33.3%) and from 7,207 to 4,982 characters (30.9%). It retains the main component boundaries, dependencies, command paths, identity relationships, and ownership responsibilities. Four peripheral trees expand parsing, edit preparation, source evidence, and runtime ownership. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] calls, [O] ownership, and [D] data dependency. Edges attach to the specific concepts being expanded; positions leave gaps between measured text bounds.

Source-grounded corrections: resolve remaps active jump source anchors, while target values pass through into the cloned view; the seed's broader wording could imply target remapping. Source-query helpers expose existing references without cloning or freezing them themselves, so their read-only contract should not be mistaken for an independent runtime immutability boundary. For patches with retainMappings, retained mappings take precedence over supplied mappings. Annotation and source-mapping edits preserve the numeric content revision while reviseDiagram issues a fresh revision identity for their new payload objects.

Details absent from the seed include WeakMap cache ownership, parser defaults and compatibility checks, multiline anchor limitations, source-binding ID derivation, evidence-range validation, edit-range precedence, and the separation between derivation ancestry and identity sources. These come only from the supplied source text. The registry, interpreter, patching helpers, and durable adapters are not supplied implementations; their internal behavior is not inferred. Flush-before-publication is shown as the supplied store comment's contract, not demonstrated persistence behavior.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the four lenses while reducing the seed from 9,906 to 6,686 characters (32.5%) and from 138 to 92 lines (33.3%). M describes modular boundaries and dependencies, C describes calls and transitions, O describes responsibility and lifetime, and D describes computational dependencies. Five peripheral trees expand meaningful central concepts rather than source-file containment.

Details beyond the seed include patch-driven section removal and collapsed-node rebasing; saved-view dirty checks, working copies and diff promotion; conversion of every source edge during a move; canonical anchor encoding; incremental change sequencing; and concrete geometry limits. These come respectively from mappingDocumentController.ts:applyOperations/updateSnapshot, canvasHistory.ts:canvasViews/openCanvasView/canvasView, canvasTransfer.ts:prepareCanvasTransfer/prepareTransferNavigation, canvasHistory.ts:encodeAnchor/documentFromHistory/persistenceChanges, and lineGrid.ts:resolveScene/layoutScene/composeScene. All are pinned sources in context.json.

Two seed generalizations are qualified: opening the already-active view stashes it and returns rather than necessarily restoring a fresh checkpoint; an empty native gesture passes through updateSnapshot, whose reference-equality exits can avoid a checkpoint. The transfer guard in the seed is confirmed: both heads must match for copy and move, although copy navigates only the destination. Move converts even edges between two unmoved placements into jumps.

External editor-driver wiring, workspace publication, revision-store internals and checkpoint-encoder internals are not supplied; the diagrams show their visible contracts and calls without inventing implementations. Positions use measured text dimensions with at least 15 columns between occupied diagram columns. All connection endpoints identify meaningful nodes using 1-based raw lines.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains 72 of the seed's 106 lines: a 32% line reduction and approximately 34% character reduction. Five connected peripherals expand ownership, gesture settlement, rendering dependencies, routing, and external calls. M, O and C describe modular structure, ownership and calls; D remains a cross-cutting computation dependency view. [shared S] identifies the controller's semantic state, with snapshots feeding rendering and checkpoint history supporting navigation.

Only the supplied definition, seed and pinned source text were used. Additional details include copy isolation and selective store publication (canvasWorkspace.ts:42-96; canvasSession.ts:69-105), selection capture and resize policies (MappingEditorRuntime.ts:132-205), projection exclusions and connection focus (shapeProjection.ts:12-51; CanvasRuntimeContext.tsx:88-179), and routing failure recovery (NativeRoutingStore.ts:68-115).

Corrections and qualifications: MappingPage.tsx:468-470 passes every non-hidden draft to the agent bridge, including inactive canvases; 'visible drafts' was imprecise. Saving captures state, synchronizes the document ID, flushes and checks the captured version before publication (912-927); sync is not passed the captured document. An unsupported native clone cancels the entire detected clone batch (MappingEditorRuntime.ts:144-147). Transfer navigation also has a projection-specific path that replaces only the child session (MappingPage.tsx:788-808). Receipt and flush behavior is method-specific: generic apply has no explicit flush in its branch (449-458).

Imported controller, persistence, bridge, worker and layout implementations are not supplied. Their internal guarantees are therefore not inferred beyond the visible calls and contracts. Positions use measured text dimensions with gaps; edge references are 1-based raw ASCII lines.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the seed's five conceptual groups while shrinking from 11,250 to 8,263 characters (26.6%) and from 153 to 98 lines (35.9%). Six peripherals expand codec mechanics, retry behavior, validation, publication, read dependencies and storage ownership. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] call flow, [O] ownership and [D] data dependency; dependency chains overlay the organizational views. Edges attach to specific concept lines. Positions use measured text bounds, with at least 18 columns between diagram columns and 7 rows between vertically adjacent peripherals.

Only context.json's point and pinned sources, plus seed.json, support the content. Source mapping: codec uses canvasCheckpointRecords.ts; retry uses recordStorage.ts and workspaceRecordStore.ts; validate uses workspaceRecords.ts; publish uses canvasCatalogStore.ts and workspaceRecordStore.ts; reads uses diagramPersistence.ts and the two stores; blobs uses workspaceRecordStore.ts, diagramRevisionStore.ts and immutableRecords.ts. The central browser bridge also uses workspacePersistence.ts.

Corrections and qualifications: CanvasValueEncoder is exported, although its caches and splitting machinery are private. The bridge method is setPaused, not pause. capture hydrates the selected head and bound revisions but pins all document checkpoint/revision/item references. loadDiagramSourceBindings passes every stored catalog revision, not only current published heads. A supplied head map bypasses replay only in loadCanvasCheckpoint; restoreCanvasCheckpoints derives maps and compares the supplied head. UI installation after acknowledgement is a documented contract, not a verified caller behavior. Catalog serialization covers wrapped operations; saveRepresentationCatalog is public and does not itself enter that queue.

Additional source details include reverse diff application, placeholder validation, interrupted-view normalization, record namespace checks, first background retry at 1000 ms, the explicit commit loop's continued retry of conflicts, acceptance receipt comparison fields and source-binding cache invalidation. Durability claims are scoped: workspace publication explicitly syncs files and directories; DiagramRevisionStore has no explicit fsync. Catalog comments describe atomic replacement, but the imported writeJsonAtomic implementation is absent, so its implementation and crash durability cannot be verified. Imported validators and catalog rules are shown only at their supplied call boundaries. No cross-process locking, blob garbage collection or unprovided UI behavior is inferred.

The central tree retains all five conceptual branches while shrinking from 93 to 61 lines (34.4%) and from 7,319 to 4,674 characters (36.1%). Five peripheral trees expand binding selection, mapped evidence, corpus boundaries, definition sessions and inspection state. [M] denotes modular structure, [C] calls, [O] ownership and [D] data dependency; [B] and [R] identify shared binding and corpus dependencies. Edges attach to the corresponding central concept lines. Tree dimensions and edge anchors were checked; positions leave nonoverlapping gaps.

Evidence comes only from the supplied point, seed and pinned source text. Binding detail follows diagramSource.ts; mapping identity and ordering follow codePanel.ts; access boundaries follow corpus.ts and projectSource.ts; lookup and lifetime detail follow projectLanguageService.ts; UI detail follows RepositoryFileExplorer.tsx and SourceCodeView.tsx. Added details include compatible binding replacement, hash-sensitive resource identity, keyboard navigation, LSP target normalization and the greater-than-240-row deferral threshold.

The seed's destination-selection description is narrowed: SourceCodeView selects only the first line of a multi-line destination, and restoration/activation guards affect when navigation runs. UTF-16 initialization accepts an omitted server encoding but rejects a different declared encoding. Session sharing is explicitly scoped to a service instance and canonical root. Returned definition targets undergo repository-path filtering, not the corpus provider's filesystem checks. Imported helper implementations and UI-to-service wiring are absent, so these trees do not infer their internal behavior or claim a verified end-to-end runtime trace.

|-- [C] Call model: representative activations across these boundaries

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the seed's conceptual coverage while shrinking from 137 to 93 lines (32.1%) and from 10033 to 6438 characters (35.8%). Five peripheral trees expand meaningful central concepts, mixing modular structure [M], calls [C], ownership [O], and data prerequisites [D]. Positions use measured text dimensions, with at least 18 columns between diagram columns and seven rows between vertically adjacent peripherals. All edge references are 1-based raw lines.

Source-grounded corrections and qualifications: (1) Projection maps live per instance. apiProjection.ts:10 states an intention to share one backend instance, but sessionService.ts:70 and liveCanvasService.ts:36 independently default to new instances; supplied construction wiring does not establish sharing. (2) Diagram-context status depends on binding and source fingerprint, while materialization supplies the payload separately (sessionService.ts:241-249). Thus the seed overstates materialized backing data as a prerequisite for status. (3) The checkpoint save flow applies without nodeId; saving one diagram instead isolates a versioned snapshot, rebases metadata and saves without canvas edges (sessionService.ts:672-714). (4) QuickJS context lifetime is one runtime invocation, including a fresh invocation during replay; retained retry state belongs to the session service. Pure-read request-cache release specifically requires a result with version and without transaction (sessionService.ts:186-188).

Peripheral additions absent from the seed include exact batch barriers and internal request prefixes (sessionService.ts:351-382), transport IDs versus mutation request IDs (canvasSessionBridge.ts:29-41; useAgentCanvasBridge.ts:43-50), copy capability negotiation and whole-diagram selection rules (liveCanvasService.ts:37-46,168-195), socket feature flags and queue limits (liveCanvasRoutes.ts:57-92), anchor capacity and jump-target membership checks (apiProjection.ts:16-41; sessionService.ts:565-585), and retained diagram-context mutation payloads (sessionService.ts:251-260).

Only the point definition, embedded pinned sources and seed were used as evidence. Imported implementations, tool HTTP route dispatch, and application construction wiring are not supplied; their internal behavior and end-to-end guarantees remain unverified. In particular, the browser hook's transport-command cache does not itself prove mutation deduplication across newly allocated dispatch IDs.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the five conceptual components while reducing the seed from 116 to 77 lines (33.6%) and from 8,478 to 5,581 characters (34.2%). Five peripherals expand validation, retry semantics, record ownership, evidence transport, and diagram identity. M = modular structure, C = call flow, O = ownership, D = data dependency; these perspectives coexist within each tree. Edges attach to the relevant central concept, and positions leave measured gaps between text rectangles.

Grounding: conversation behavior comes from domain/core/agents/agentContext.ts; library and retry behavior from application/mapping/agent/agentContextLibrary.ts and domain/core/agents/savedAgentContext.ts; publication and locking from infrastructure/core/persistence/fileAgentContextRepository.ts; capture and transport from infrastructure/core/persistence/fileAgentContextSources.ts; diagram identity from domain/core/diagrams/diagramAgentContext.ts. Only the supplied point, sources, and seed were used as evidence.

Corrections and qualifications: trajectory cycle/missing-link checks cover the traversed ancestor slice, not the entire trajectory. The seed's stale-comment-hash failure claim needs an exception: an identical existing comment receipt returns before checking the current snapshot hash. Diagram loading validates backing identity but does not compare the saved fingerprint or revision against current evidence; the point's change-detection claim therefore requires caller behavior absent from these inputs. The background message requests the current diagram on later edits, but these files do not establish that callers supply it. Source-file checks use the 16 MiB constant despite stale 2 MiB error text and comments. Portable conversion recomputes the hash but need not change its value.

New peripheral details include missing-attachment acceptance during snapshot validation, repeated expansion byte accounting, noncanonical request hashing, cache eviction order, source-ID fallback, and full-record reads behind summaries. Implementations of imported source-range helpers, ImmutableRecords, and session-launch callers are not supplied; their internals and end-to-end session behavior remain unverified.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 119 to 76 lines and from 8,334 to 5,336 characters: approximately 36% less by either measure. Five peripheral trees expand meaningful concept nodes. M denotes modular boundaries and dependencies, C execution, O ownership, and D computational prerequisites; D is a dependency view rather than another organizational category. Positions account for actual text dimensions and leave gaps.

Source-grounded corrections: variant generation belongs before installation (diagramEditService.ts:187-216), rather than under installation as in the seed. The seed's 'canvas.batch once' means one combined application per attempt: a matching acknowledgement retry invokes batch again with retained output (diagramBatchService.ts:27-30,101-108). Extension requires an explicit origin, so automatic placement is a creation fallback, not an extension option (diagramEditService.ts:72,276).

Additional details include reference lookup and excerpt rules, context identity exceptions, saved variant scope and decision resets, context chaining for multi-create but not variants, batch revision supplementation and placement offsets, submission field forwarding, and workflow hook ordering. These come from the seven source texts pinned in context.json, particularly diagramEditService.ts:127-159,179-204,225-243; diagramBatchService.ts:58-84; generateDiagram.ts:5-12; diagramEditRuntime.ts:33-95; validatedSubmission.ts:19-42; agentRuntime.ts:35-68; and agentWorkflow.ts:24-51.

Limits: imported domain validators and concrete canvas implementations are not supplied, so their internal validation, persistence and deduplication behavior cannot be established here. The create port explicitly documents request-ID idempotency; retained outputs and stable request IDs alone do not prove equivalent transport guarantees for apply/batch. No restart recovery or workflow invocation from the supplied diagram runtime is shown.

The central tree shrinks from 114 to 75 lines (34.2%) and from 8,920 to 5,737 characters (35.7%). It retains modular boundaries, call paths, ownership and cross-cutting data dependencies. Four peripheral trees expand meaningful concepts: request submission, edit preparation, transcript delivery and isolated candidate state. M = modular structure, C = call, O = ownership, D = data dependency. Positions leave gaps between actual text rectangles; edges use 1-based raw lines.

Only context.json and seed.json supplied evidence. Source-grounded corrections and qualifications: agentChatRoutes.ts:8-27,54-90 limits tool previews to SSE snapshots, rather than all session responses; its generation projection removes history but leaves inputHistory. generationCanvasBridge.ts:33-89 implements only a subset of CanvasSessionPort, including restricted view behavior. AgentChatService.finishGeneration at agentChatService.ts:319-340 saves the terminal child before entering the synchronization try/finally, so the seed's cleanup statement is conditional: failure of that save can bypass cleanup. startTurn at :410-459 records request IDs before submission without removing them on failure; duplicate suppression does not establish successful execution.

Additional details absent from the seed include SSE backlog allowance and preview thresholds, subtree-selection completeness checks, preparation-cache limits, transport-derived projection retry identity, and mutation receipts retained before persistence. These come from agentChatRoutes.ts:23-90, chatDiagramTools.ts:75-112,216-267, and generationCanvasBridge.ts:40-91. Panel retry and stream ownership follow AgentChatPanel.tsx:140-217.

Uncertainty: imported implementations such as ChatStore, ChatStream, the controller and evaluation observer are not supplied. Their internals are not inferred. Lifecycle failure observations describe visible control flow, not experimentally reproduced failures.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree retains the five functional boundaries while shrinking the seed from 113 lines/8,960 characters to 77 lines/6,013 characters: reductions of 31.9% and 32.9%. Five peripheral trees expand pinned push resolution, workflow lifetime, capture/mutation, review recovery, and split persistence. M = modular structure, C = calls, O = ownership, D = data dependency. Tree nesting groups concepts; it does not imply execution order unless stated. Edges attach to specific concept lines, using 1-based line numbers. Positions account for measured text dimensions and leave gaps.

Evidence is limited to the supplied point, seed, and six pinned source texts. Push details come from pushIntegrationService.ts and gitPushSource.ts; workflow ownership from diffSessionWorkflowService.ts; capture, mutation, review, and acceptance from changeSessionService.ts; persistence and validation from changeSessionRecords.ts and diagramChangeSession.ts. Added details absent from the seed include replay preceding push enablement checks, Git execution settings, endpoint comparison with empty commit lists, separate API receipt queues, four-preview batches, manifest token contents, and hunk-context validation.

Corrections: capture skips unrelated repository documents before requesting snapshots; it rejects a repository mismatch detected after snapshotting. The service performs final validation after runAgentWorkflow returns, rather than treating validation as another agent step. History/tree/migration edits initially set draft, but an explicit ready status in the same update revalidates and can finish ready. Existing push deliveries can replay before enablement checks, which govern new generation. The public boundaries now include connections and request, omitted from the seed.

Uncertainty: imported workflow definitions, DiffSessionTools, catalog publication, and immutable-record helpers are not supplied. Their internal scheduling, transaction guarantees, and persistence mechanics cannot be independently established here. The diagrams show observed calls, arguments, checks, and receipt recovery; they do not claim verified catalog atomicity. The workflow source identifies analyze/materialize stage names, while the exact step definition remains imported.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree reduces the seed from 134 to 94 lines (29.9%) and from 9,847 to 6,686 characters (32.1%). Six peripheral trees expand meaningful concept lines: interface state, frozen inputs, execution, experiment attempts, comparison evidence and output retention. [M] = modular structure; [C] = call flow; [O] = ownership/lifetime; [D] = data dependency across those organizational views. Positions use measured text dimensions, leaving at least 10 columns between bands and five rows between stacked peripherals. Edge lines are 1-based.

Evidence is limited to the point definition and eight source texts in context.json, with seed.json as the starting tree. New details include polling revision guards and intervals (EvalsPage.tsx:70-97), merge ancestry and stage-only hashing (evalPromptService.ts:14, 131-164), checkpoint revision boundaries (compareSessionService.ts:32-42), runtime isolation and cache-key composition (agentContextEvalRuntime.ts:18-35), planned-cell coverage and judgement ownership (experimentService.ts:58-99), and stricter placement-backfill requirements (evalRunService.ts:153-175).

Corrections and qualifications: 'relaunch selected stage' can imply stage-only execution, but launchEdited requests the workflow with one ordinary pass and experiment relaunch remaps matching stages (evalRunService.ts:295-300, 441-443; experimentService.ts:208-215). The diagrams therefore say workflow rerun. The seed's blanket late-response guarantee is narrowed to usePolled's closed guard; it suppresses updates without aborting the request. Mixed success becomes partial only after queued/generating cells are gone (evalRun.ts:94-99). Judgement run/cell links are optional when reconciliation cannot resolve ownership (judgementService.ts:31-35). Public API labels use setArchived and deleteRun. Validation retries cover validator failures; runtime exceptions escape that loop (evalRunService.ts:654-668).

Imported implementations outside the supplied texts remain dependency boundaries. The internal few-shot algorithm, validator/materializer behavior, base session persistence and catalog publication atomicity are not established here. The result passes output-schema.json validation; ASCII, edge endpoints and diagram non-overlap were checked.

discovery.summary: The architectural center is an immutable Diagram revision model composed into versioned canvases. Browser editing, agent tools, isolated change proposals, and evaluation workflows converge on shared canvas commands and history, while filesystem adapters publish durable records. Fifteen anchors capture these responsibilities, their ownership boundaries, and the separate static-analysis tooling. Review depth varied: every inventoried file received a source-text structural skim, with implementation-level tracing concentrated on these anchors.

points.title: Application Composition and Transports
points.rationale: The server bootstrap selects concrete repositories, agent runtimes, and services, connects their ports, and disposes their resources. The Vite adapter mounts HTTP and WebSocket interfaces. Architecture tests enforce the domain/application/infrastructure/UI boundaries, making this the clearest entry point for understanding dependency direction.

relationships.label: constructs and injects filesystem repositories
wires canvas bridges and mounts agent transports
constructs chat service and disposes its connection
connects generation, comparison, and experiment services

points.title: Immutable Diagram Revisions
points.rationale: Diagram is the shared content boundary: stable diagram identity, immutable revision identity, ASCII content, source evidence, mappings, highlights, and jumps travel together. Revision operations validate edits and preserve explicit node continuity; the registry rejects conflicting payloads under an existing identity. Canvas placement remains outside this content model.

relationships.label: builds and validates parsed content and node identities

points.title: ASCII Structure and Anchors
points.rationale: This boundary turns ASCII into addressable structure used by selection, folding, source mapping, and connection endpoints. Parser versions preserve compatibility with stored content. Tree content carries its parsed structure, while graph content exposes a cached derived node index; the spatial interpreter retains source spans and interpretation evidence.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: MappingDocumentController is the common mutation facade for live editing and headless proposals. CanvasHistory owns checkpoints, diagram revision bindings, branching, undo/redo, and saved views. Commands validate versions and complete their changes before publishing a checkpoint. LineGrid separates reusable diagram content from hierarchical placements and layout.

relationships.label: retains issued revisions through checkpoint bindings
uses content nodes to validate and reconcile anchors

points.title: Browser Workspace Ownership
points.rationale: CanvasWorkspace owns canvas session lifetimes; each CanvasSession exposes separate subscriptions for document, presentation, selection, controls, geometry, and status. WorkspacePersistence translates committed changes into incremental records, while RecordStorage coalesces writes and retries ambiguous failures with the identical request. This explains how many open canvases share persistence without publishing every pointer movement.

relationships.label: creates session controllers and retains editing contexts
sends versioned record batches through workspace HTTP
mounts an editor for each canvas session

points.title: Native Canvas Interaction
points.rationale: The tldraw Editor owns live geometry and native undo navigation. MappingEditorRuntime projects semantic state into shapes and commits settled gestures back to the controller. CanvasRuntime keeps renderer-local models, measurements, connection focus, and routing resources. This is an important ownership boundary between interactive frames and durable semantic changes.

relationships.label: commits gestures and restores semantic checkpoints
consumes the mounted canvas session
uses revision-scoped nodes for rendered anchors

points.title: Durable Records and Publication
points.rationale: Persistence distinguishes the editable workspace from published catalog representations. WorkspaceRecordStore writes content-addressed records before atomically replacing a manifest containing revision guards and retry receipts. Catalog publication can pin an already persisted checkpoint without expanding its entire archive. DiagramStore supplies the shared repository facade.

relationships.label: persists checkpoint graphs, composition, and view records
stores immutable revisions before publishing references

points.title: Repository Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source resolution follows an explicit diagram source binding instead of assuming a project has one repository. Mapping joins resolve selected diagram nodes to captured source ranges, retaining provenance and hashes. Corpus and language-service adapters provide file access and definition lookup, while CodePanel translates these joins into the browsing experience.

relationships.label: resolves source bindings, mappings, and captured evidence
reads registered sources and published representations

points.title: Agent Canvas Access
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService binds tool operations to specific canvases or proposals, resolves compact read aliases, enforces access modes, and handles retries. CanvasSessionBridge dispatches commands to browser owners; LiveCanvasService tracks publishers, selection deltas, and reader identities. MCP and HTTP expose this shared application boundary.

relationships.label: dispatches commands to the owning browser workspace
routes proposal-scoped reads and mutations
starts diagram edits and atomic generation batches
resolves uploaded and saved agent contexts

points.title: Reusable Agent Contexts
points.rationale: AgentContext is a validated, hashed conversation value with coherent tool-call history and pinned source references. AgentContextLibrary manages durable creation, forks, comments, and discovery. Source adapters choose committed Git content or immutable snapshots and can produce portable selected-range exports. This is the reusable input boundary shared by editing and evaluations.

relationships.label: captures source ranges through repository and corpus bindings
binds compiled context to diagram identity and source fingerprint

points.title: Validated Diagram Generation
points.rationale: DiagramEditService pins target revisions, resolves prompt references and contexts, generates candidates, and applies them only through a version-checked canvas port. Batch generation stages multiple operations before one application. The runtime accepts output through a validating submission tool and owns cancellation and session cleanup; issuing a revision remains a domain operation.

relationships.label: validates candidate edits and issues immutable revisions
loads pinned context and captures successful conversation history
uses supplied canvas ports for snapshots and acknowledged application

points.title: Agent Chat Lifecycle
points.rationale: AgentChatService owns persistent conversations, turn deduplication, streaming events, pending questions, and turn-bound canvas access. StdioCodexConnection owns the external app-server process and RPC lifecycle. GenerationCanvasBridge gives background alternatives isolated controller-backed canvases, allowing chat generation to reuse canvas operations without editing the live source canvas.

relationships.label: invokes tools with the canvas captured for the active turn
owns isolated controllers for generation candidates
reuses saved context for background generation

points.title: Isolated Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository commits, hunks, and canvas baselines into isolated proposals. Proposal edits use the shared controller and retain their own history and receipts. Acceptance checks both live and published baselines before publishing affected canvases. The two-step workflow and push integration provide automated entry paths into this review boundary.

relationships.label: applies proposal edits through isolated controller histories
publishes accepted canvases with durable acceptance receipts
pins repository context and captures Git hunks
exposes scoped tools to the materialization workflow

points.title: Generation Experiments and Evaluation
points.rationale: EvalRunService coordinates repeatable workflows over pinned canvas inputs, prompt versions, references, and AgentContexts. ExperimentService prepares and launches reviewed plans; comparison capture preserves selected checkpoints independently of later source changes. Materializers turn validated model output into canvases, while judgements and promotion connect evaluation results back to published work.

relationships.label: pins context hashes and resolves model-visible evidence
captures checkpoints and materializes generated canvases
publishes promoted outputs into the project catalog
reconciles chat-generated alternatives into evaluation runs

points.title: Static Architecture Analysis
points.rationale: A separate CLI-driven pipeline extracts declarations, lexical references, calls, resource ownership, framework relationships, and dataflow from TypeScript. It derives partitions, metrics, components, and findings with source provenance. IncrementalAnalyzer owns reusable component fragments and broadens invalidation for uncertain global effects. This is a substantial independent subsystem, not an established browser generation stage.

relationships.label: shares source-layer classification with architecture boundary tests

limitations: This was not a complete line-by-line reading of the 7.28 MB snapshot. reviewedPaths includes files inspected through source-text excerpts: declarations, imports, method names, test descriptions, or opening statements. Detailed implementation reading concentrated on the selected architectural paths; many leaf components, tests, styles, scripts, benchmarks, Python parser utilities, and projection-3d files received only a structural skim.
Relationships describe source-supported dependencies and invocation paths, not observed runtime traces. Tests and the application were not executed.

The assessment is limited to the pinned working-tree snapshot. The index excludes corpus data, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor dependencies, node_modules, most documentation, binary assets, and lockfiles.
Secondary responsibilities such as file compaction, local selection chat, search, treemaps, migrations, and the 3D prototype remain expansion candidates rather than separate initial anchors.

canvas.explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 140 lines/9353 characters to 92 lines/6189 characters: 34.3% fewer lines and 33.8% fewer characters. Six peripherals expand meaningful central nodes. Modular boundaries organize the central tree; command execution adds call relationships, history and transfers expose ownership, and anchors expose data dependencies. Positions use measured text widths and heights with gaps; all diagrams are connected and edge lines are 1-based.

Evidence is limited to the point definition, embedded sources in context.json, and seed.json. Peripheral details go beyond the seed: empty native gestures and deferred move layout in MappingDocumentController; lazy checkpoint validation and mutable transaction metadata in CanvasHistory; exact layout ordering and coordinate conversion in LineGrid; generation identity checks; and transfer behavior for unselected edges.

Source-grounded qualifications: CanvasHistory.openCanvasView only stashes when the requested view is already active, so opening does not always restore a fresh checkpoint. The seed's absolute checkpoint immutability wording is narrowed: linkTransaction and retireTransactions replace transaction metadata under existing checkpoint IDs. CanvasTransfer converts ALL source edges into jumps during move, including edges whose endpoints are both unselected; it checks both history boundaries even for copy. The workspace publication claim is presented as an external contract documented by canvasTransfer.ts, since the workspace implementation is absent. Similarly, checkpoint publication after validation does not establish rollback of every revision-helper effect during staging. The imported transfer-placement algorithm and revision-helper internals are not supplied and remain unspecified.
